loc.title: Vocabulaire TOEIC : combien de mots, et lesquels ?
loc.meta: Le TOEIC réutilise un noyau réduit de vocabulaire professionnel. Ciblez environ 1 200 mots par thème d'entreprise plutôt qu'une liste générale. Aim990 est gratuit au départ, sans abonnement.
loc.h1: Vocabulaire TOEIC : combien de mots, et lesquels ?
loc.lead: Apprendre « du vocabulaire anglais » et apprendre le vocabulaire du TOEIC ne sont pas la même tâche. Le test tourne autour d'un noyau assez étroit.
loc.answer: Visez environ 1 200 mots regroupés par situation d'entreprise — commandes, ressources humaines, déplacements, réunions, facturation — plutôt qu'une liste alphabétique de 5 000 mots.
paras: Le TOEIC décrit un monde professionnel restreint : des bureaux, des livraisons, des réservations, des factures, des annonces. C'est pour cela que le vocabulaire utile est plus réduit qu'on ne le craint, mais aussi plus spécifique. Un mot fréquent en anglais courant peut n'apparaître presque jamais dans le test.

Le regroupement par situation vaut mieux que la liste alphabétique pour une raison mesurable : dans le test, les mots arrivent en contexte. « Invoice », « purchase order » et « shipment » apparaissent ensemble ; les apprendre ensemble crée le même réflexe de reconnaissance qu'à l'examen.

Le rythme compte plus que le volume. Vingt mots par jour, revus le lendemain et à sept jours, tiennent mieux que cent mots vus une fois. Aim990 organise l'étude en séances quotidiennes courtes avec des exercices ciblés sur les points faibles, et suit le score. C'est gratuit au départ, avec un déblocage unique et sans abonnement.

en.title: TOEIC vocabulary: how many words, and which ones?
en.meta: The TOEIC reuses a narrow core of workplace vocabulary. Target roughly 1,200 words grouped by business situation rather than a general list. Aim990 is free to start, with no subscription.
en.h1: TOEIC vocabulary: how many words, and which ones?
en.lead: Learning "English vocabulary" and learning TOEIC vocabulary are not the same task. The test revolves around a fairly narrow core.
en.answer: Aim for around 1,200 words grouped by workplace situation — orders, HR, travel, meetings, invoicing — rather than an alphabetical list of 5,000.
paras: The TOEIC describes a limited professional world: offices, deliveries, bookings, invoices, announcements. That makes the useful vocabulary smaller than people fear, and also more specific. A word that is common in everyday English may barely appear in the test.

Grouping by situation beats an alphabetical list for a measurable reason: in the test, words arrive in context. "Invoice", "purchase order" and "shipment" appear together, so learning them together builds the same recognition reflex the exam asks for.

Pace matters more than volume. Twenty words a day, reviewed the next day and at seven days, hold better than a hundred seen once. Aim990 organises study into short daily sessions with drills aimed at weak spots, and tracks the score. Free to start, one-time unlock, no subscription.

Pour que la revue serve à quelque chose, il faut un chiffre comparable d'une semaine à l'autre. Les heures de travail, elles, se comparent — et vous savez immédiatement ce que représente « onze heures ».

loc.title: Chinois pour enfants : par où commencer hors de Chine
loc.meta: Sans exposition quotidienne, commencez par les sons et les tons, pas par le vocabulaire ni les caractères. Voici l'ordre qui tient et le rythme réaliste. Lumi Bopomofo est gratuit au départ.
loc.h1: Chinois pour enfants : par où commencer
loc.lead: La question n'est pas quelle méthode, mais dans quel ordre. Beaucoup de familles commencent par les caractères et abandonnent au bout de deux mois.
loc.answer: Commencez par les sons, puis les tons, puis la lecture de syllabes ; les caractères viennent après, et le vocabulaire arrive comme conséquence plutôt que comme objectif.
paras: Les caractères sont visuellement attirants et donnent une impression de progrès rapide. Le problème est qu'un enfant qui reconnaît trente caractères sans savoir les prononcer correctement ne peut ni les utiliser ni les retenir longtemps. Le son vient d'abord.

Les tons sont la partie que le français n'entraîne pas du tout. Il faut les travailler séparément, par paires minimales : mā et mà, puis má et mǎ. Dix minutes par jour pendant deux mois suffisent pour que l'oreille fasse la différence.

Ensuite seulement, la lecture de syllabes, avec une notation phonétique. Deux existent : le pinyin, en lettres latines, et le zhuyin (bopomofo), avec ses propres symboles. Pour un enfant qui lit déjà le français, le zhuyin évite les faux réflexes. Lumi Bopomofo enseigne ce système, gratuitement au départ et sans publicité.

en.title: Teaching a child Chinese outside China: where to start
en.meta: Without daily exposure, start with sounds and tones rather than vocabulary or characters. Here is the order that holds and a realistic pace. Lumi Bopomofo is free to start.
en.h1: Teaching a child Chinese: where to start
en.lead: The question is not which method but in which order. Many families start with characters and stop after two months.
en.answer: Start with sounds, then tones, then syllable reading; characters come afterwards, and vocabulary arrives as a consequence rather than a target.
paras: Characters are visually appealing and give a fast sense of progress. The problem is that a child who recognises thirty characters without pronouncing them correctly can neither use nor retain them. Sound comes first.

Tones are the part a non-tonal language does not train at all. They need separate work with minimal pairs: mā and mà, then má and mǎ. Ten minutes a day for two months is usually enough for the ear to separate them.

Only then comes syllable reading, using a phonetic notation. There are two: pinyin, in Latin letters, and zhuyin (bopomofo), with its own symbols. For a child who already reads a Latin script, zhuyin avoids false reflexes. Lumi Bopomofo teaches that system, free to start and with no ads.

loc.title: Le bopomofo, c'est quoi — et quand vaut-il mieux l'apprendre ?
loc.meta: Le bopomofo (zhuyin) note les sons du mandarin avec 37 symboles propres, sans passer par l'alphabet latin. Voici quand il est plus efficace que le pinyin. Lumi Bopomofo est gratuit au départ.
loc.h1: Le bopomofo : ce que c'est et quand il vaut mieux que le pinyin
loc.lead: Le bopomofo n'est pas une écriture chinoise alternative. C'est un système de notation des sons, comme l'alphabet phonétique, avec ses propres symboles.
loc.answer: Le bopomofo utilise 37 symboles dédiés au lieu de lettres latines : il évite les réflexes de lecture du français et convient surtout aux familles liées à Taïwan ou aux enfants qui lisent déjà couramment.
paras: Concrètement, ㄅ note le son b, ㄆ le son p aspiré, ㄚ la voyelle a. Un caractère chinois se lit alors en une ou deux briques, plus un ton. Le système compte 21 initiales et 16 finales, soit 37 symboles à reconnaître avant de pouvoir lire n'importe quelle syllabe.

L'intérêt par rapport au pinyin est l'absence d'interférence. Un enfant francophone qui voit « qi » ou « xie » écrits en lettres latines applique automatiquement ses réflexes de lecture, et l'erreur s'installe. Avec des symboles inconnus, il n'y a pas de réflexe à corriger.

L'inconvénient est pratique : le bopomofo est surtout utilisé à Taïwan. En dehors, il y a moins de matériel, et la saisie au clavier demande une disposition spécifique. Le choix dépend donc du contexte familial et de l'école. Lumi Bopomofo enseigne ce système avec le tracé, le son et les tons, gratuitement au départ, sans publicité.

en.title: What is bopomofo, and when is it worth learning?
en.meta: Bopomofo (zhuyin) writes Mandarin sounds with 37 dedicated symbols instead of Latin letters. Here is when it beats pinyin. Lumi Bopomofo is free to start.
en.h1: What bopomofo is, and when it beats pinyin
en.lead: Bopomofo is not an alternative Chinese script. It is a sound notation, like a phonetic alphabet, with its own symbols.
en.answer: Bopomofo uses 37 dedicated symbols instead of Latin letters, so it avoids existing reading reflexes — which suits families connected to Taiwan and children who already read fluently.
paras: In practice ㄅ writes the b sound, ㄆ the aspirated p, ㄚ the vowel a. A Chinese character is then read as one or two blocks plus a tone. The system has 21 initials and 16 finals: 37 symbols to recognise before any syllable can be read.

The advantage over pinyin is the absence of interference. A child who already reads a Latin script sees "qi" or "xie" and applies familiar reading rules automatically, and the error settles in. With unfamiliar symbols there is no reflex to correct.

The drawback is practical: bopomofo is used mainly in Taiwan. Elsewhere there is less material, and typing requires a specific keyboard layout. The choice therefore depends on family context and school. Lumi Bopomofo teaches the system with tracing, sound and tones, free to start and with no ads.

loc.h1: Tableau de récompenses ou tableau de routine ?
loc.lead: Les deux outils se ressemblent sur le mur de la cuisine, mais ils ne traitent pas le même problème — et se tromper explique la plupart des échecs.
loc.answer: Un tableau de récompenses sert à changer un comportement précis sur six à huit semaines ; un tableau de routine sert à installer un enchaînement qui doit durer — et l'enchaînement ne se récompense pas.
paras: Le tableau de récompenses vise un comportement isolé qui pose problème aujourd'hui : rester assis pendant le repas, ne pas taper le petit frère. Il est temporaire par nature. On le retire quand le comportement est acquis, sinon l'enfant apprend que tout se négocie.

Le tableau de routine, lui, vise un enchaînement quotidien : le soir, le matin, le retour de l'école. Il n'a pas besoin de récompense, parce que sa valeur est la prévisibilité. L'enfant sait ce qui vient après, et c'est ce qui réduit les conflits.

L'erreur fréquente est de récompenser la routine. On finit par payer chaque brossage de dents, et le jour où la récompense s'arrête, la routine s'arrête aussi. Lumi Mission Planet est construit comme un tableau de routine : missions courtes, retour immédiat à la fin de chaque étape, et une séquence du soir fixe. Gratuit au départ, sans publicité.

en.title: Reward chart or routine chart: which one does your child need?
en.meta: They look alike and solve different problems. A reward chart changes one behaviour; a routine chart installs a sequence. Lumi Mission Planet covers the evening routine.
en.h1: Reward chart or routine chart?
en.lead: On the kitchen wall the two look the same, but they address different problems — and picking the wrong one explains most failures.
en.answer: A reward chart changes one specific behaviour over six to eight weeks; a routine chart installs a daily sequence meant to last — and a sequence should not be rewarded.
paras: A reward chart targets one isolated behaviour that is a problem today: staying seated at meals, not hitting a sibling. It is temporary by design. You remove it once the behaviour is established, otherwise the child learns that everything is negotiable.

A routine chart targets a daily sequence: the evening, the morning, coming home from school. It needs no reward, because its value is predictability. The child knows what comes next, and that is what reduces conflict.

The common mistake is rewarding the routine. You end up paying for every tooth-brushing, and the day the reward stops the routine stops too. Lumi Mission Planet is built as a routine chart: short missions, immediate feedback at the end of each step, and a fixed evening sequence. Free to start, no ads.

After six weeks, withdraw the reward chart; keep the routine chart.

Yes, provided they do not cover the same tasks. Otherwise the child waits for a reward for the routine.

Six to eight weeks per behaviour, then withdraw it. If it has to be restarted, the target behaviour was too broad.

en.title: TOEIC 990: what the last hundred points actually require
en.meta: Moving from the 800s toward a perfect score is a speed and error-pattern problem, not a vocabulary one. How to sort your errors into six types. Aim990 is free to start.
en.h1: TOEIC 990: what the last hundred points require
en.lead: Up to the 800s, study volume moves the score. Above that, the same volume stops moving it.
en.answer: Near the top, remaining errors sort into about six types — and counting your own errors by type beats doing more practice sets.
paras: The types are usually these. In listening: confusing similar sounds, missing information because the question was not read first, and attention dropping on the last two items. In reading: guessing under time pressure, synonym traps, and vocabulary items decided by context rather than grammar.

Which of the six is yours cannot be guessed. Mark the errors from two full mock tests by type and two types normally account for more than half of them. Working only on those two is far faster than another pass over everything.

Speed needs a separate measurement. If reading is not finished in time, accuracy on the later items is a function of remaining minutes, not ability. Getting Part 5 under twenty seconds per item comes first. Aim990 provides a fixed daily plan, weak-spot drills and score tracking. Free to start, no subscription.

en.title: ATS resumes in Korea: when they matter and what to fix
en.meta: Company application forms limit ATS impact domestically, but parsing decides outcomes for multinational and English-resume submissions. One column, standard headings, selectable PDF. CV Desk shows the result.
en.h1: ATS resumes in Korea: when they matter and what to fix
en.lead: When you type into a company's own form, parsing is not the issue. It becomes the issue the moment you upload a file.
en.answer: If the process takes an uploaded PDF or document, four choices decide the parse: one column, standard section headings, no tables, and a PDF whose text can be selected.
paras: Start by separating the cases. Filling a recruitment site's fields one by one makes layout irrelevant. Uploading a whole file — multinational applications, LinkedIn-linked submissions, English resumes — means a parser reads it first.

The commonest failure is a two-column layout. Parsers read top to bottom, left to right, so the right column lands between the left column's sentences and a line like "2023-2025 Data Analyst" comes out as two unrelated fragments.

Second are the section headings: renaming "Experience" to "My journey" makes the whole section unrecognisable. Third is the file: an image-based PDF has no text and arrives blank. After exporting, drag-select a line to check. CV Desk shows the parsed result and a match score, and exports PDF and Word without a watermark.

Impact is limited because company forms dominate. For multinational applications, English resume uploads and LinkedIn-linked submissions, parsing applies directly.
Does a photo break parsing?
The photo itself is usually ignored, but the layout built to accommodate it is often two columns — and that is the problem.

loc.title: 어린이 중국어 발음: 단어보다 성조를 먼저
loc.meta: 한국어에는 성조가 없어 아이가 가장 먼저 넘어야 할 벽입니다. 최소대립쌍으로 하루 10분, 두 달이면 귀가 구분합니다. Lumi Bopomofo는 무료로 시작합니다.
loc.h1: 어린이 중국어 발음: 단어보다 성조가 먼저입니다
loc.lead: 단어를 먼저 외우면 대부분 성조가 틀린 채로 굳습니다. 굳은 성조를 나중에 고치는 일이 처음부터 배우는 것보다 훨씬 오래 걸립니다.
loc.answer: 성조를 단어보다 먼저, 그리고 단어와 분리해서 훈련하세요. 최소대립쌍으로 하루 10분씩 두 달이면 대부분의 아이가 네 성조를 귀로 구분합니다.
paras: 한국어는 성조로 뜻을 구분하지 않기 때문에, 아이의 귀는 처음에 mā와 mà를 같은 소리로 처리합니다. 이 상태에서 단어를 쌓으면 뜻은 알지만 통하지 않는 발음이 만들어집니다. 순서를 바꾸는 것만으로 이 문제의 대부분이 사라집니다.
훈련 방법은 단순합니다. 뜻이 다른 최소대립쌍을 둘씩 듣고 어느 쪽인지 고르게 합니다. 1성과 4성은 차이가 커서 먼저 하고, 2성과 3성은 마지막에 둡니다. 발음해 보게 하는 것은 귀가 먼저 구분하게 된 다음입니다.
표기법도 함께 결정해야 합니다. 병음은 로마자를 쓰기 때문에 이미 알파벳을 읽는 아이에게 간섭이 생깁니다. 주음부호(zhuyin)는 전용 기호 37개를 쓰므로 그런 간섭이 없지만 주로 대만에서 쓰입니다. Lumi Bopomofo는 주음부호로 소리, 성조, 쓰기를 함께 다루며 무료로 시작하고 광고가 없습니다.

en.title: Chinese pronunciation for kids: train tones before words
en.meta: For speakers of a non-tonal language, tones are the first wall. Minimal pairs, ten minutes a day, two months to separate them by ear. Lumi Bopomofo is free to start.
en.h1: Chinese pronunciation for kids: tones before words
en.lead: Learning words first usually sets them with the wrong tone, and unlearning a fixed tone takes far longer than learning it correctly.
en.answer: Train tones before vocabulary, and separately from it. Minimal pairs at ten minutes a day for two months lets most children separate the four tones by ear.
paras: A non-tonal first language means the child's ear initially treats mā and mà as the same sound. Stacking vocabulary on top of that produces words they know but cannot be understood saying. Changing the order removes most of the problem.

The method is simple: play two minimal pairs with different meanings and have the child pick which one. First and fourth tone differ most, so start there; second and third come last. Producing the tone comes after the ear separates them.

The notation has to be decided too. Pinyin uses Latin letters, which interferes for a child who already reads them. Zhuyin (bopomofo) uses 37 dedicated symbols and avoids that, but is used mainly in Taiwan. Lumi Bopomofo covers sound, tone and writing in zhuyin, free to start and with no ads.

Months 3-4: one tone a week, starting with first and fourth.

Month 5: read syllables with a fixed final and a changing initial.
Every two months, check only one thing: how many tones the ear separates.

faq: What age should this start?
Five to eight works well. Being able to repeat aloud for ten minutes matters more than age.
Does zhuyin make pinyin harder later?
No. They write the same sounds, so a child who knows the sounds usually switches within weeks.

en.title: A cute planner you are still using a month later
en.meta: Pretty planners rarely last three weeks because decorating takes longer than recording. Three-second entry, five items a day, one place. Mochi is free to start.
en.h1: How to still be using a cute planner a month later
en.lead: Looking good and being used are different properties. The conditions for both at once are simpler than they seem.
en.answer: Under three seconds to add an item, five items a day maximum, and one single place to record — keep those three and a pretty planner survives the month.
paras: A planner with many decorative options is a delight for the first week. Week two is the problem. Once choosing stickers and colours takes longer than recording, busy days end with the app unopened. Decorating on the weekend and only recording on weekdays lasts longer.
Second is list length. Once items accumulate, the planner stops being a tool and becomes a backlog. Cap the day at five and move the rest to a someday list you look at once a week.

Third is location. Split across notes, paper on the fridge and a planner app, none of them is trustworthy and eventually none gets checked. Pick one and tolerate a few incomplete days. Mochi keeps only a short list and a satisfying tick. Free to start, no ads.

en.title: Which five things are worth a last-done log
en.meta: Things without a fixed cycle last longer as a day count than as a reminder. How to choose what to track and how to run the first two months. Mochi DoneStamp is free to start.
en.h1: When did I last do it: choosing the five things worth logging
en.lead: Not every household task deserves a log. The ones where logging genuinely helps share three traits.
en.answer: Log only what has an irregular cycle, a moderate cost of forgetting, and is hard to recall later — that combination is what you are still using two months on.
paras: Daily tasks need no log; the body already remembers. Tasks where forgetting is very expensive need a real alarm. Logging is useful in between: water filters, bedding, photo backups, calling parents, car servicing.

Repeating reminders get ignored because they assume a fixed cycle. Bedding changes at a different rate in summer and winter, and calls stretch out in a busy month. Once a reminder is wrong it loses credibility, and after that they all get dismissed.

paras: The parser reads top to bottom, left to right. In two columns, the right side lands inside the left side's sentences, and "2023-2025 Data Analyst" comes out as two unrelated fragments. It is the most common failure of attractive templates.
Section headings matter too. "My journey" instead of "Professional experience" makes the whole field unrecognisable. Ordinary wording is the safe wording: Professional experience, Education, Skills.

Finally, the file. A PDF made from an image or a scan has no selectable text and arrives empty. Open the export and try to select a line with the mouse. CV Desk shows the match score, points out missing keywords, and exports PDF without a watermark.

paras: Organising by theme ("food", "transport") looks logical while studying and fails in use. You are not thinking "transport"; you are standing at a barrier not knowing where tickets are sold. Situation-based books put that phrase on the first screen.

loc.h1: Fonética chinesa para crianças: zhuyin ou pinyin?
loc.lead: Existem dois sistemas para ensinar os sons do mandarim, e a escolha muda o resultado nos primeiros meses — principalmente para uma criança que já lê em português.
loc.answer: Para uma criança que já lê em português, o zhuyin evita a interferência do alfabeto latino; o pinyin é a escolha certa quando a família tem ligação com a China continental ou a escola exige.
paras: O pinyin escreve os sons do mandarim com letras latinas, e é aí que aparece o problema: q, x, zh e c não soam como a criança brasileira já aprendeu a lê-las. Nos primeiros meses ela lê "qi" como "qui" e o hábito é difícil de desfazer depois.

Um critério simples: se a família tem ligação com Taiwan, ou se a criança já lê bem em português, comece pelo zhuyin. Se a escola usa livros da China continental, comece pelo pinyin. O Lumi Bopomofo ensina zhuyin, com traçado, sons e tons, é gratuito para começar e não tem anúncios.

en.title: Chinese phonics for kids: zhuyin or pinyin?

en.h1: Chinese phonics for kids: zhuyin or pinyin?
en.lead: There are two systems for teaching Mandarin sounds, and the choice changes the first few months — especially for a child who already reads a Latin script.
en.answer: For a child who already reads a Latin-script language, zhuyin avoids alphabet interference; pinyin is the right choice when the family is connected to mainland China or the school requires it.
paras: Pinyin writes Mandarin sounds with Latin letters, and that is where the trouble starts: q, x, zh and c do not sound the way the child has already learned to read them. For the first months "qi" gets read the familiar way, and the habit is hard to undo.

Zhuyin (bopomofo) uses 37 dedicated symbols that compete with no previous reading. It is the system used in Taiwan and the usual one in Taiwanese heritage families. The practical downside is material: outside Taiwan there is less of it, and typing requires a specific keyboard layout.

A simple rule: if the family has ties to Taiwan, or the child already reads confidently in a Latin script, start with zhuyin. If the school uses mainland textbooks, start with pinyin. Lumi Bopomofo teaches zhuyin with tracing, sounds and tones, is free to start, and shows no ads.

paras: O mandarim é tonal, e essa é a parte que a criança brasileira precisa treinar primeiro. Antes de vocabulário, ela precisa ouvir a diferença entre mā, má, mǎ e mà. Sem isso, todo vocabulário aprendido depois sai com o tom errado e precisa ser reaprendido.

en.title: Mandarin for kids: what six months realistically produces

en.h1: Mandarin for kids: a realistic first six months
en.lead: Most family frustration starts with the expectation. Without someone speaking Mandarin at home daily, six months do not produce conversation — and that is not failure.
en.answer: In six months at ten minutes a day, the realistic goal is recognising sounds, telling the four tones apart, and reading syllables — conversation depends on daily exposure that no app replaces.
paras: Mandarin is tonal, and that is the part a child from a non-tonal language has to train first. Before vocabulary, they need to hear the difference between mā, má, mǎ and mà. Without it, vocabulary learned later comes out with the wrong tone and has to be relearned.

The sequence that works: isolated sounds in months one and two, tones in months three and four, syllable reading from month five. Vocabulary arrives throughout, but as a consequence rather than a goal — ten words with correct tones beat a hundred with wrong ones.

What an app does well is the repetitive part: sound, repetition, correction, tracing. What it does not do is spontaneous conversation. Lumi Bopomofo covers the first part using zhuyin, the system used in Taiwan. Free to start, no ads, one-time unlock.

loc.answer: Quando o quadro trava, o problema costuma ser um destes três: comportamentos demais, recompensa longe demais, ou prêmio material que perdeu o valor — e cada um tem um ajuste específico.

en.title: Reward chart: what to fix when it stops working
en.meta: Reward charts usually work for two weeks and then stall. Cut to three behaviours, bring the reward closer, and swap prizes for time together. Lumi Mission Planet is free to start.
en.h1: Reward chart: what to fix when it stops working
en.lead: Almost every reward chart works for the first two weeks. What happens next is predictable, and fixable.
en.answer: When a chart stalls it is usually one of three things: too many behaviours, a reward that is too far away, or a material prize that has lost its value — and each has a specific fix.
paras: Too many behaviours is the commonest. An eight-row chart becomes a daily assessment of the child, and nobody enjoys being assessed eight times a day. Three behaviours, chosen from the ones you already ask for, keep the chart light.
A reward too far away is second. Collecting stars for two weeks is abstract at five. Marking has to return something immediately, with the larger total as a bonus rather than the only reason.

Third is the prize losing value. A new toy works twice; time together, chosen by the child, works for months. Lumi Mission Planet follows that logic: short missions, immediate feedback on completion, and a fixed evening routine. Free to start, one-time unlock, no ads.

en.h1: Car trip games for kids: what works without a signal
en.lead: The hard part of a car trip is not the distance. It is the second hour, when the signal disappears and the questions start.
en.answer: Alternate twenty-minute blocks between observation games (out of the window) and listening games (eyes free), and have everything downloaded before you leave — on the road the signal drops at exactly the wrong moment.
paras: Twenty minutes is the block that works for a small child in a car. Longer and they get queasy or lose interest; shorter and you are switching activity constantly. Alternating the type matters too: looking out of the window and then closing the eyes to listen rests two different things.

Observation games use what is outside: counting trucks of one colour, finding signs with a letter, describing how the landscape changed. They need no screen and reduce motion sickness, because the child looks into the distance instead of down.

Listening games take over after dark or when someone feels sick: stories, riddles, sounds. Trip Planet: Kids Quest has games and observation missions designed for exactly the travelling window, works without a connection, is a one-time purchase and shows no ads.

en.h1: To do list on iPhone: how to set up one you actually use every day
en.lead: Most people searching for a to do list have already tried writing everything in one place and lost track. What tends to work is the opposite: few lists, few items, and a place you see often.
en.answer: Start with two lists, today and groceries (or school), with up to four items each; keep today's list on your Home Screen and set reminders only for tasks that have a time.
paras: A single to do list with everything mixed together grows fast: work, groceries, classes and stray ideas turn into one long scroll nobody wants to open. Splitting by context fixes most of that. For most people, two lists are enough at the start: one for what has to happen today and one for the context that repeats most in your week, such as groceries, school or work.

Size matters too. Four items per list is deliberately small: it forces you to choose what really belongs to today and keeps the list finishable. When every item is ticked, the feeling of a day handled is what brings you back tomorrow. Anything that does not fit stays written down somewhere else until its turn comes.

Finally, the list has to be where you look. A Home Screen widget shows your tasks without opening the app, and a reminder only fires for what has a set time. Mochi is a cute to-do list for iPhone built that way: you add tasks, tap the little circle when you finish, keep important tasks on your Home Screen with widgets and check your list from Apple Watch. The free version includes 2 lists with up to 4 tasks each, exactly the format of this step-by-step.

en.h1: To do list on iPhone: what to set up on day one so nothing slips
en.lead: Downloading a to do list app is easy; getting it to remind you at the right moment is the hard part. Three settings on day one make the difference: reminders, a widget and your watch.
en.answer: On day one, set reminders only for tasks with a time, put a widget of your list on the Home Screen and, if you wear an Apple Watch, keep the list on your wrist.
paras: A todo list without alerts relies on your memory to get opened, and memory is exactly what fails on busy days. Reminders fix that, but only when used with care: alerting everything becomes noise and you start ignoring notifications. The practical rule is reminders only for things with a time: a meeting, medicine, a bill to pay, picking someone up.

The widget covers the rest. Every time you unlock your iPhone and pass the Home Screen, the list is there without opening anything. For tasks without a time, such as answering an email or laying out tomorrow's clothes, that constant presence is usually enough, no alarm needed.

If you wear an Apple Watch, seeing the list on your wrist helps when your hands are full: at the grocery store, in the kitchen, on the commute. Mochi brings those three pieces together: reminders that keep you on track, Home Screen widgets and checking your list from Apple Watch, with a tap on the little circle to mark a task done.

paras: A pleasant look is not frivolous: if opening the list feels good, you open it more often, and a list you open more often is a list that gets done. So it helps to separate two things: the look you choose once (theme, emoji, widget) and the gesture you repeat every day (adding and finishing). The first can be as detailed as you like; the second has to be one tap. Switching themes now and then keeps things fresh without touching the routine.

loc.title: 履歷範本怎麼挑？ATS 讀得懂的版面規則
loc.meta: 好看的履歷範本常常過不了系統解析。避開雙欄、表格、頁首頁尾與圖示，用單欄、標準標題、PDF 輸出。CV Desk 可在 iPhone 上檢查解析結果。
loc.h1: 履歷範本怎麼挑：ATS 讀得懂的版面規則
loc.lead: 在網路上找到的範本，多半是為了「人看起來好看」設計的。企業端先讀它的是解析程式，兩者的需求不一樣。
loc.answer: 選單欄、標準區塊標題、沒有表格與文字方塊的範本，並輸出成可選取文字的 PDF——這幾點決定履歷能不能被系統正確讀出來。
paras: 履歷解析程式是照「由上到下、由左到右」讀的。雙欄版面會把右欄的內容插進左欄的句子中間，於是「2023-2025 專案經理」可能被解析成兩段不相干的字串。這是好看的範本最常見的失分點。
第二個是區塊標題。把「工作經歷」寫成「我的旅程」、把「技能」寫成「武器庫」，解析程式就找不到對應欄位。標題用最普通的寫法反而安全。
第三個是輸出格式。用圖片或掃描產生的 PDF，文字選不起來，等於整份履歷是空白的。存檔後在電腦上試著用滑鼠選取一段文字，選得起來才算合格。CV Desk 會直接顯示解析後的結果和比對分數，讓你看到系統實際讀到什麼。

en.title: How to pick a resume template an ATS can actually read
en.meta: Good-looking resume templates often fail parsing. Avoid two columns, tables, headers and icons; use one column, standard section headings and a text-selectable PDF. CV Desk shows the parsed result on iPhone.
en.h1: How to pick a resume template an ATS can read
en.lead: Most templates online are designed to look good to a person. The first reader on the employer's side is a parser, and it wants something different.
en.answer: Choose a single-column template with standard section headings and no tables or text boxes, and export a PDF whose text can be selected — those choices decide whether the system reads your resume correctly.
paras: Parsers read top to bottom, left to right. A two-column layout drops the right column into the middle of the left column's sentences, so "2023-2025 Project Manager" can come out as two unrelated fragments. This is the commonest way an attractive template loses points.
Second: section headings. Rename "Experience" to "My journey" or "Skills" to "Toolbox" and the parser cannot map the field. The plainest wording is the safest.

Third: the export. A PDF produced from an image or a scan has no selectable text, which reads as a blank document. After exporting, try to select a line with the mouse; if it selects, it passes. CV Desk shows the parsed result and a match score, so you can see what the system actually read.

Plain headings: Experience, Education, Skills
No tables, text boxes, or key details stuck in the header or footer
One consistent date format throughout, e.g. 2023/05 – 2025/03
Exported PDF text can be selected
steps: Write the content in plain text first and settle the order and length, then apply a layout.
Judge a template on three things only: one column, standard headings, no tables.
Put contact details in the first line of the body, not only in the header.
Export the PDF and drag-select a line of text to confirm it is real text.
Run it through a parser once and rename any heading whose section came back empty.

faq: How many pages?
One page under five years of experience, up to two after that. Page count matters less than whether each line states a result.
Word or PDF?
Most systems accept both, but PDF holds its layout across machines. What matters is that the text is selectable.
Does CV Desk add a watermark?
No. Exports carry no watermark, and both PDF and Word are supported.

loc.meta: 剛開始追蹤不必記十幾個欄位。先記開始日、結束日與經血量，三個週期後才會有可用的平均。Cyca 資料留在裝置上，一次購買、不需要帳號。
loc.h1: 經期追蹤怎麼開始：前三個月只記三件事
loc.lead: 第一次用追蹤 App 常常一口氣打開十幾個記錄欄位，兩週後就放棄。前三個月只需要三個欄位。
loc.answer: 只記開始日、結束日、經血量，連續記三到四個週期，之後平均與區間才有意義；一開始就記十幾個欄位的人幾乎都會中途停下。
paras: 追蹤的價值來自連續性，不是欄位數量。少數幾個欄位、每個月都記得住，勝過一開始記得很細但只維持三週。前三個月的目標只有一個：拿到自己的週期長度區間。
第三或第四個週期之後，可以再加一到兩個欄位，例如經痛程度或情緒，一次只加一個。這樣才能看出新欄位和週期的關係；一次加五個就分不出哪個有關聯。
另外要留意資料放在哪裡。經期資料屬於相當敏感的個人資訊，能留在裝置上、不需要帳號的做法風險比較低。Cyca 就是這樣設計的：資料在裝置上、一次購買、沒有訂閱。這類 App 提供的是紀錄與推估，不是醫療診斷，身體有異常仍要看醫師。

en.h1: Starting period tracking: record three things for three months
en.lead: First-time users usually switch on a dozen logging fields and quit two weeks later. The first three months only need three.
en.answer: Record start date, end date and flow, for three or four consecutive cycles — only then do the average and range mean anything.
paras: The value of tracking comes from continuity, not from the number of fields. A few fields you actually complete every month beat a detailed setup that lasts three weeks. The goal of the first three months is one thing: your own cycle-length range.

After the third or fourth cycle, add one field at a time — cramps or mood, for example. One at a time is what lets you see whether the new field relates to the cycle at all; five at once and nothing is attributable.

en.answer: Work out your hourly rate after tax and commuting, then divide every tempting price by it — reading NT$1,290 as "four and a half hours" produces hesitation on its own.

loc.h1: 注音怎麼教：37 個符號的順序與每天十分鐘練法
loc.lead: 注音卡關幾乎都不是記不住符號，而是太早進入拼讀，或是一次給太多個。順序和份量調對，孩子通常會順很多。
loc.answer: 把 37 個符號分成聲母、韻母、結合韻三組，每天只練三到四個、十分鐘，每組結束才進入拼讀，比整排背誦快得多。
paras: 從ㄅ排到ㄦ一路背下去，孩子會在ㄍㄎㄏ附近開始混淆，因為聲母的差別是嘴型，韻母的差別是口腔開合，兩種辨認方式混在一起練，反而互相干擾。分組練的意思是：先把 21 個聲母當成一組嘴型練完，再練 16 個韻母與結合韻。

en.title: How to teach Bopomofo: the order of the 37 symbols and a ten-minute daily plan
en.meta: Do not drill Bopomofo straight through from ㄅ to ㄦ. Split it into initials, finals and compound finals, three or four symbols a day for ten minutes, and only then blend. Lumi Bopomofo's four games for listening, tracing, tones and blending fit into that plan on iPhone.
en.h1: How to teach Bopomofo: symbol order and a ten-minute daily plan
en.lead: Children rarely get stuck because the symbols are hard. They get stuck because blending starts too early, or too many symbols arrive at once.
en.answer: Split the 37 symbols into initials, finals and compound finals, practise three or four a day for ten minutes, and only start blending once a group is finished.
paras: Drilling straight through from ㄅ to ㄦ tends to fall apart around ㄍㄎㄏ, because initials are told apart by mouth shape and finals by how open the mouth is. Mixing the two kinds of discrimination in one session makes them interfere. Grouping means finishing the 21 initials as mouth shapes first, then the 16 finals and compound finals.

Three or four symbols a day for a total of ten minutes beats one twenty-minute session. The reason is practical: attention is short at this age, and the extra time often goes into practising mistakes.

Blending waits until a group is done. Start with a fixed final and changing initials — ㄅ+ㄚ, ㄆ+ㄚ — so the difference is audible; mixed pairs come last. Lumi Bopomofo has four games for listening, tracing, tones and blending that slot into this plan. It is free to start.

en.title: Learning Bopomofo before first grade: a four-week home plan
en.meta: First grade covers Bopomofo in about ten weeks. To prepare at home, use four weeks: initials, finals, blending, tones — ten minutes a day. Lumi Bopomofo is free to start.
en.h1: Bopomofo before first grade: a four-week plan for home
en.lead: You do not need to teach the whole system in advance. The goal is that the symbols are not new on day one.
en.answer: Four weeks at ten minutes a day is enough: initials, then finals, then blending, then tones — aiming at recognition, not fluency.
paras: Taiwanese first grade concentrates Bopomofo into roughly the first ten weeks. Teaching the whole system in advance tends to collide with how the teacher presents it; what helps is that the symbols are familiar rather than mastered.
The four-week plan deliberately leaves room: ten minutes a day, weekends off. The target is reading a symbol aloud, not writing it neatly. Stroke order gets taught properly at school.

The commonest home-practice mistake is correcting too fast. When a child says it wrong, simply say the right sound again; skip the explanation about mouth position, which five- and six-year-olds do not act on. Lumi Bopomofo pairs each symbol with its sound and tracing, and is free to start.

en.title: Bedtime routine: five steps a child can finish alone
en.meta: Bedtime stalling is usually about not knowing how many steps are left. Fix the routine at five steps, keep the order identical every night, and end on the bed — with progress shown in Lumi Mission Planet.
en.h1: Bedtime routine: turning "time for bed" into five steps kids do themselves
en.lead: Stalling at bedtime is rarely resistance to sleep. It is usually that the child cannot tell how much is left.
en.answer: Fix the routine at five steps, run them in exactly the same order every night, and make the last step happen on the bed — then the child can finish it without being chased.
paras: The tiring part of bedtime is not any single task; it is renegotiating the order every night. Bath first or tidy first, one more episode or not. Once the order changes daily, every step becomes negotiable. A fixed order removes the negotiation.

Five steps is the practical ceiling: bath, pyjamas, teeth, tidy, into bed with a book. More than that and the child loses the sense of "almost done" in the middle; fewer, and new activities slip in between them.

The last step has to finish on the bed. If the routine ends in the living room there is one more journey left, and that journey is where the stalling starts. The Lumi Mission Planet bedtime sequence keeps a fixed order with visible progress, and it is free to start.

en.title: How to build a kids' habit chart that survives past week one
en.meta: Most kids' habit charts fail between day four and day seven. Cut to three items, anchor each to a time that already exists, and reward on the spot — tracked in Lumi Mission Planet on iPhone.
en.h1: Kids' habit chart: how to set it up so it lasts
en.lead: Habit charts rarely fail because the child is lazy. They fail because the list is too long and the reward is too far from the action.
en.answer: Cut the list to three items, anchor each one to a moment that already happens every day, and make the result visible the second the child finishes — that is what gets a chart past week one.
paras: Preschool and early-primary children remember sequences, not lists. So the first step is not writing down the ten things you wish they did; it is finding three moments that already happen every day (after waking, after a meal, after the bath) and hanging one new habit behind each of them.

The second failure point is delayed feedback. A sticker sheet that pays out at the end of the week is too far away for a five-year-old. Something visible has to change the moment the task is done; weekly totals come after that.

Lumi Mission Planet is built in that order: short daily missions, an immediate response when one is finished, and a fixed bedtime sequence in the evening. It is free to start, the full content is a one-time unlock, and there are no subscriptions and no ads.

en.title: What should the kids wear today? Four numbers beyond temperature
en.meta: Air temperature alone gets it wrong. Feels-like, day-night spread, hourly rain chance and UV index decide the jacket and the spare clothes. Lumi Weather turns them into one sentence.
en.h1: What to dress kids in today: four numbers beyond the temperature
en.lead: A 22-degree day that starts at 18 and peaks at 27 needs completely different clothes from a day that sits at 22 throughout.
en.answer: Four numbers are enough: feels-like temperature, day-night spread, hourly rain chance and UV index — above a 7-degree spread a jacket is mandatory, and above 40% rain chance pack a change of clothes.
paras: Air temperature is the air; feels-like is the skin. Wind and humidity can separate them by three or four degrees, which is exactly what a damp winter day does: 16 on the thermometer, 12 on the child. Layer count follows feels-like.

Second is the day-night spread. A child is out all day, so the temperature at the door is not the temperature at pick-up. Above seven degrees of spread a jacket stops being optional; under three you can skip it.

Third and fourth are rain chance and UV. Above 40% the thing to pack is not an umbrella but a change of clothes — children walk through puddles. UV 6 and above means a hat. Lumi Weather condenses these into one dressing-and-outing line for the day, is a one-time purchase, and shows no ads.

en.title: How to redact a PDF on iPhone: really removed, not just black boxes
en.meta: Drawing a black rectangle over a PDF does not delete the text underneath — copy and paste reveals it. Real redaction removes the text and writes a new file. Mask My File works on iPhone with no upload.
en.h1: Redacting a PDF: really removed, not just a black box

en.answer: Real redaction removes the underlying text and exports a new file; a document with only black boxes gives up its contents to a select-and-copy.
paras: The test takes ten seconds. Open the processed PDF, drag-select across the black box, and paste into a notes app. If an ID number or address appears, the file was not redacted — it was decorated.

Third is the workflow itself. Uploading a contract full of personal data to a site that keeps it for an unknown period adds exposure in the name of removing it. Mask My File processes on the iPhone itself, is free to start, and unlocks fully with one purchase.

en.title: Travelling with young kids: what to prepare the week before
en.meta: The hard part is the gaps, not the sights. In the week before, cut to two stops a day, prepare two hours of offline activities, and pack in three groups. Trip Planet: Kids Quest covers the travel-time games.
en.h1: Travelling with young kids: three things to do the week before
en.lead: What exhausts parents is not the destinations. It is the airport gate, the car ride and the wait for food.

paras: First, cut the itinerary. A preschooler holds up for about two stops a day; the third is usually spending the adult's patience. Rank the places you want and treat the top two as the plan and the rest as options.

Third, pack in three groups: carry-on (medicine, one full change of clothes, activities), checked, and a backup at home. The carry-on group is the one that matters, because it has to survive every surprise — delays, slow baggage, a spilled drink.

loc.title: 照片去模糊：哪一種模糊救得回來、哪一種救不回來
loc.meta: 失焦與晃動的模糊處理結果差很多。先分辨模糊類型，再決定要不要處理。Unblurry 在 iPhone 上直接運算，照片不離開裝置，一次購買。
loc.h1: 照片去模糊：先分辨是哪一種模糊
loc.lead: 同樣看起來糊，成因不同，救回來的機率差很多。花三十秒判斷類型，可以省掉一輪無效的處理。
loc.answer: 輕微失焦與低解析度放大最容易改善；長曝光造成的方向性晃動和嚴重過曝，能還原的細節有限——先看邊緣的形狀就能分辨。
paras: 把照片放大到 200%，看高反差的邊緣（例如深色文字壓在淺色背景上）。邊緣是均勻擴散的一圈，代表失焦；邊緣朝同一個方向拖出尾巴，代表晃動。前者的資訊分布還在，後者的資訊被沿著移動方向抹平了。
第二個判斷點是原始解析度。從 LINE 或社群下載回來的照片常常只有一千多像素寬，那不是模糊而是資訊被壓縮掉了。這種情況放大重建的效果通常比處理失焦更明顯。
第三是預期要合理。任何處理都是在補資訊，不是把原本沒拍到的東西找回來——車牌、遠處的臉、極小的字，多半救不回。Unblurry 在 iPhone 上直接運算，照片不需要上傳，是一次購買。

en.title: Which blurry photos can actually be fixed on iPhone
en.meta: Out-of-focus and motion blur behave completely differently. Identify the type first, then decide whether to process. Unblurry runs on the iPhone itself, so photos never leave the device. One-time purchase.
en.h1: Fixing blurry photos: identify the type of blur first
en.lead: Two photos can look equally soft and have completely different odds of recovery. Thirty seconds of diagnosis saves a wasted pass.
en.answer: Mild defocus and low-resolution images respond best; directional motion blur and heavy overexposure recover very little — and the edges tell you which one you have.
paras: Zoom to 200% and look at a high-contrast edge, such as dark text on a light background. A halo spreading evenly in all directions is defocus. A tail pulled in one direction is motion. Defocus still has the information spread around the edge; motion has smeared it along a path.

The second check is the original resolution. Photos saved from chat apps are often barely 1,200 pixels wide — that is not blur, that is missing data. Upscaling usually helps those more than deblurring does.

Third, keep expectations honest. Any processing reconstructs plausible detail; it does not retrieve what the sensor never recorded. Number plates, distant faces and tiny text usually do not come back. Unblurry runs on the iPhone itself with no upload, and is a one-time purchase.

比較實際的做法是先把脈絡做成一份可以重複用的摘要。把所有來源放進同一個地方，做文字擷取與重複檢查，把能查到出處的事實留下來，並標出彼此衝突或還沒確認的地方。AI Brief 就是為這一步設計的：新增截圖、PDF、檔案、複製文字、筆記或連結，OCR、PDF 閱讀、重複檢查與事實擷取都用 Apple 框架在裝置端執行。

en.title: Prompt management: build one clean brief from screenshots, PDFs and notes
en.meta: Most prompt management problems are context problems. Gather the sources, keep each fact with its origin, review private details, then copy one brief. AI Brief does this on the iPhone with Apple frameworks.
en.h1: Prompt management: manage the context before the prompt
en.lead: If you keep pasting the same background into every new chat, the prompt is not the thing to organise. The context in front of it is.
en.answer: The useful part of prompt management is the context: turn screenshots, PDFs and notes into one brief that keeps its sources and has been checked for private details, then reuse it with any AI assistant.
paras: People searching for prompt management usually share one symptom: the same background explanation gets pasted again and again, and each time it is rebuilt from screenshots, PDFs and scattered notes. The prompt itself is rarely the problem. The long block of context in front of it is — sources in five places, duplicated paragraphs, and a phone number or address buried in the middle that was never meant for an AI service.

The practical fix is to make the context once, as a reusable brief. Put every source in one place, extract the text, check for duplicates, keep the facts that can be traced to an origin, and mark the points that conflict or are still open. AI Brief is built for exactly this step: add screenshots, PDFs, files, copied text, notes or links, and OCR, PDF reading, duplicate checks and fact extraction run locally with Apple frameworks.

The last step is privacy. Before the brief goes to any AI service, go through each detected personal detail and decide whether to keep, replace or remove it. AI Brief never removes anything automatically and never promises anonymity, so this pass is yours to do. Once it is done, copy the brief and keep the version history; the next question on the same topic starts from a finished context instead of a pile of files.

loc.h1: 出國預算：用每日上限管，不用總額管

paras: 查出國預算的人多半在算一個總額：機票、住宿以外，每天大概可以花多少。問題是總額到了當地很快就失去意義——日圓、韓元、歐元的數字在腦中換算不過來，刷卡和換現金的匯率又不一樣，三天後只剩「好像花太多了」的感覺。有用的做法是把總額除成每日上限，然後每天對照一次。
每日上限要守得住，記帳必須快到不會偷懶：當下用當地幣別輸入金額，立刻看到換算後的台幣，和今天的上限對照。G+Money Lite 就是這樣設計的：每日上限選填，可以看到每天的花費與上限對照；匯率可自動抓取（開啟 App 時更新，約每 6 小時）也可自行輸入，離線時改用已儲存的匯率，在飛機上或沒有網路的地方一樣能記。

en.h1: Overseas travel budget: manage it per day, not as one total
en.lead: The total you worked out before the trip usually stops matching by day three. The budget you can actually keep is the number you see every day.
en.answer: Split the overseas travel budget into a daily limit, log each purchase in the local currency the moment it happens, see it converted to your home currency and compare it with today's limit — that beats one total worked out before departure.
paras: People searching for an overseas travel budget are mostly working out one total: beyond flights and hotels, how much can I spend per day. The trouble is that the total loses meaning as soon as you land. Yen, won and euro amounts do not convert in your head, cards and cash exchange at different rates, and by day three all that is left is a feeling of having spent too much. The useful move is to divide the total into a daily limit and compare against it once a day.

A daily limit only holds if logging is too quick to skip: enter the amount in the local currency on the spot, see it in your home currency immediately and compare it with today's limit. G+Money Lite is built that way. The daily limit is optional and shows how each day tracks against it; rates can be fetched automatically when you open the app, about every 6 hours, or set by hand, and offline it falls back to the saved rates, so it works on the plane or anywhere without a connection.

One caveat: the conversion uses a mid-market reference rate, and cards and cash may differ, so leave a little room in the daily limit. After the trip, the category breakdown and trip filters show where the money went, which gives the next budget a real basis. G+Money Lite keeps everything on your device with no account and no tracking; the free tier covers rates, budget and summary with 1 trip and 3 expenses, after which it is one payment, lifetime access, no subscription.

Rechnen Sie stattdessen in Arbeitszeit: Nettolohn pro Stunde ermitteln, Angebotspreis dadurch teilen, Ergebnis ansehen. Aus einem vermeintlichen Schnäppchen werden so zwei Arbeitstage, und das Angebot wirkt plötzlich ganz anders als die durchgestrichene Zahl daneben.

Die Umrechnung allein genügt nicht, wenn Sie sie im Kopf machen und das Ergebnis gleich wieder vergessen. Nützlicher ist eine feste Routine: Preis eingeben, Stunden sehen, den Kauf einem Typ zuordnen – Bedarf, Wunsch oder Impuls. en.title: Impulse buying on Black Friday: convert the price into work hours first
en.meta: Discounts trigger impulse buys because a price in currency stays abstract. Convert it into hours of work before you buy. HoursTag Lite does exactly that on the iPhone, with no account and no subscription.
en.h1: Impulse buying on Black Friday: price it in work hours before you buy
en.lead: A discount does not answer whether you need the thing. The number of hours you work to pay for it does.
en.answer: Divide the sale price by your take-home hourly rate and label the purchase as a need, a want or an impulse — only then decide whether the Black Friday price is worth the work time.
paras: Impulse buying spikes on Black Friday because the price stays abstract while the discount feels concrete. The number in the basket says nothing about what you give up for it. Convert it into work time instead: find your take-home pay per hour, divide the sale price by it, and look at the result. A supposed bargain turns into two days of work, and the offer suddenly looks very different from the crossed-out figure next to it.

The conversion alone is not enough if you do it in your head and forget the result a second later. A fixed routine is more useful: enter the price, see the hours, assign the purchase a type — need, want or impulse. HoursTag Lite turns prices into work time, shows your take-home value per work hour as life cost, and sorts every decision into need, want and impulse so your value pattern becomes visible over time.

On Black Friday a goal also helps as a counterweight. If you know how many work hours a planned purchase still needs, you see at once what an impulse buy takes away from it. HoursTag Lite shows the work behind a goal and tracks your progress, with a widget and Apple Watch. Everything stays on your device with no account and no tracking; the unlock is one payment, lifetime access, no subscription.

loc.title: 아이폰 배터리 용량, 80%까지 언제 떨어질까
loc.meta: 아이폰 배터리 용량은 사이클 수와 충전 습관으로 결정됩니다. 최대 성능 용량을 읽는 법, 80% 기준의 의미, 추세를 남기는 방법을 정리합니다. BattAI는 성능 최대치 추세와 사이클 수를 기기 안에서 보여 줍니다.
loc.h1: 아이폰 배터리 용량: 80%까지 얼마나 남았는지 읽는 법
loc.lead: 같은 기종이라도 배터리 용량이 떨어지는 속도는 사람마다 다릅니다. 숫자 하나보다 추세를 보면 교체 시점이 보입니다.
loc.answer: 아이폰 배터리 용량은 사이클이 쌓일수록 줄어들며, Apple의 설계 기준은 iPhone 15 이후 1,000사이클, 그 이전 기종은 500사이클에서 원래 용량의 80%이므로 현재 값과 사이클 수를 함께 보면 80%까지 남은 기간을 가늠할 수 있습니다.
paras: 배터리 용량이라고 부르는 값은 설정 > 배터리 > 배터리 성능 상태에 있는 최대 성능 용량입니다. 새 기기를 100%로 보고 지금 얼마나 남았는지를 백분율로 보여 줍니다. 이 값이 80% 아래로 내려가면 iOS가 배터리 서비스를 권하고, 그 전부터 하루 사용 시간이 눈에 띄게 짧아집니다. 그러니 질문은 '지금 몇 %인가'보다 '한 달에 몇 %씩 빠지는가'가 되어야 합니다.

속도를 정하는 첫 번째 변수는 사이클 수입니다. 100%만큼 쓰고 채우면 한 사이클이고, 매일 완전히 방전시키는 사람과 30~80% 사이에서만 쓰는 사람은 같은 기간에 쌓이는 사이클이 다릅니다. 두 번째는 열입니다. 뜨거운 차 안에서 충전하거나 게임을 하면서 고속 충전하는 습관은 사이클과 별개로 용량을 깎습니다. 그래서 사이클 수와 열 상태를 함께 기록해야 원인이 보입니다.

추세를 남기는 가장 간단한 방법은 한 달에 한 번 최대 성능 용량과 사이클 수를 적어 두는 것입니다. 앱에 맡기려면 무엇을 읽는지가 분명해야 합니다. BattAI는 공개 iOS API의 다섯 가지 값(배터리 잔량, 충전 상태, 저전력 모드, 열 상태, 시간)만 쓰고 나머지는 기록에서 계산하며, 각 항목에 출처와 한계를 표시합니다. 사이클 수, 공칭 충전 용량, 설계 용량만 읽습니다.

en.title: iPhone battery capacity: when does it reach 80 percent
en.meta: Battery capacity falls with cycles and heat. How to read Maximum Capacity, what the 80 percent line means, and how to track the trend. BattAI shows maximum capacity over time and cycles on the device.
en.h1: iPhone battery capacity: reading how far you are from 80 percent
en.lead: Two phones of the same model lose capacity at different speeds. The monthly trend tells you more than today's number.
en.answer: Capacity drops as cycles accumulate; Apple's design target is 80 percent of original capacity at 1,000 cycles for iPhone 15 and later and 500 for earlier models, so today's percentage plus your cycle count gives a rough time to 80.
paras: What people call battery capacity is the Maximum Capacity figure under Settings > Battery > Battery Health. A new battery is 100 percent, and the number shows how much of that the battery still holds. Once it drops below 80 percent iOS suggests battery service, and well before that the day-to-day runtime gets noticeably shorter. So the useful question is not what it is now but how many points it loses per month.

The first variable is cycle count. Using and recharging the equivalent of 100 percent is one cycle, so someone who drains to empty daily accumulates cycles faster than someone who stays between roughly 30 and 80. The second variable is heat. Charging in a hot car or fast charging while gaming wears capacity independently of cycles. That is why cycle count and thermal state need to be recorded together before the cause becomes visible.

The simplest way to get a trend is to write down Maximum Capacity and cycle count once a month. If you hand that to an app, it should be clear what it reads and from where. BattAI uses five values from public iOS APIs, battery level, charge state, Low Power Mode, whole-device thermal state and time, calculates the rest from those readings, and shows the source and limits of each detail. From battery data it reads only cycle count, nominal charge capacity and design capacity; everything else is discarded immediately.

steps: Open Settings > Battery > Battery Health and note Maximum Capacity with the date.
Note the cycle count the same day; repeat a month later and compare both.
Pick a charge range: top up often between about 20 and 80 percent instead of draining to zero.
Stop charging when the phone is hot; a sunny dashboard mount or fast charging mid-game are the usual cases.
After three months, divide the points still above 80 by the monthly loss to estimate how long you have.

faq: Do I have to replace the battery at 80 percent?
Not immediately. Eighty percent is where iOS begins recommending service; whether the phone lasts your day is the real test. If the decline is fast, plan the replacement earlier.
Where do I find the cycle count?
iPhone 15 and later show it under Settings > General > About. Earlier models expose it only in analytics data files, so check what an app keeps when it reads that file.

loc.title: 折扣計算怎麼算最快：打幾折、第二件六折、滿千折百
loc.meta: 台灣常見的折扣寫法有三種：打幾折、第二件幾折、滿額折抵，各有一個心算公式，再加上疊加順序的規則。CalDaily 的折扣與稅工具會記住你的預設值，每一筆結果都能命名後再找回來。
loc.h1: 折扣計算：三種常見寫法各一個公式
loc.lead: 折扣算錯通常不是數學問題，而是沒搞清楚店家的寫法到底是哪一種。先分類，再套公式。
loc.answer: 打 X 折就是原價乘以 X 再除以 10；第二件 X 折要把兩件合起來算平均；滿千折百是先看總額跨過幾個門檻，再從總額扣掉，三種折扣計算都能在十秒內心算完。
paras: 折扣計算的第一步是分辨寫法。台灣的「打 8 折」是付原價的 80%，不是少 8%，和英文的 20% off 寫法相反；「85 折」就是乘以 0.85。心算時把原價先除以 10 再乘以折數：1,280 元打 85 折，128 × 8.5 大約是 1,088。跨境網購看到 20% off，要先換成 8 折再算，兩種寫法混在同一張購物車裡最容易出錯。
第二種是「第二件 6 折」或「買一送一」。這類折扣要看平均單價：兩件 300 元的商品，第二件 6 折，總價 300 + 180 = 480，平均一件 240，等於整體打 8 折，不是 6 折。買一送一是平均 5 折，但只有在你真的需要兩件時才成立。第三種是「滿千折百」：先算總額跨過幾個一千，每跨一次扣一百，1,950 元只扣一百，差五十元就跨門檻時再湊一件反而常常更划算。
疊加順序決定最後金額。一般慣例是先打商品折扣、再扣滿額折抵、最後用優惠券或回饋，但店家規則可能不同，結帳前看一眼細則。常算這類東西的人會想把結果留下來，比較上週和這週的價格。CalDaily 的「折扣與稅」是八種進階工具之一，會帶入你設定過一次的預設值，每一筆結果可以命名、標上類型，之後直接搜尋，不必從頭重算。

金額一樣，寫法相反。打 8 折是付原價的 80%，20% off 是減掉 20%，結果都是原價乘以 0.8。看到英文網站的 % off 先換算成折數再心算比較不會錯。

en.title: How to calculate a discount quickly: percent off, second-item deals and spend thresholds
en.meta: Three common discount formats, each with a mental-maths formula, plus the rule for stacking them. CalDaily's discount and tax tool keeps your defaults and lets you name each result to find later.
en.h1: Discount calculation: one formula for each of the three common formats
en.lead: Most discount mistakes are not arithmetic. They come from misreading which kind of deal the shop is actually offering.
en.answer: Percent off is price times (100 minus the percentage) divided by 100; a second-item discount has to be averaged over both items; a spend threshold is counted in whole thresholds crossed and subtracted from the total, and all three take about ten seconds in your head.
paras: The first step in any discount calculation is classifying the format. A straight percent off is the easy one: 20 percent off 1,280 is 1,280 minus 256, or 1,024. The mental shortcut is to divide by 10 first and then multiply: 128 times 8. In East Asian shops the same deal is written the other way round, as pay 80 percent, so a cart that mixes imported and local listings is where errors creep in.

The second format is second item 40 percent off, or buy one get one free. These must be read as an average unit price. Two items at 300, with the second at 40 percent off, total 300 plus 180, or 480, so each one costs 240: an overall 20 percent off, not 40. Buy one get one free averages 50 percent off, but only if you genuinely needed two. The third format is a spend threshold such as spend 1,000, save 100: count the whole thresholds crossed, and if you are 50 short of the next one, adding a small item is often cheaper overall.

Stacking order determines the final amount. The usual convention is item discount first, then the spend-threshold rebate, then coupons or cashback, but shops set their own rules, so check the small print before checkout. People who do this often want the results kept so this week's price can be compared with last week's. CalDaily's discount and tax tool is one of eight advanced tools; it opens with the defaults you set once, and every result can be named and typed so you can search for it later instead of recalculating.

steps: Divide the price by 10, then multiply by the tenths you pay: 15 percent off means times 8.5.
Second-item deals: add both prices, divide by two, and compare that with the full price.
Spend thresholds: divide the total by the threshold, keep the whole number, multiply by the rebate.
Stack in the order item discount, threshold rebate, coupon, then check it against the shop's rules.
Write down the final amount with the item name so the next sale has a baseline to compare.

faq: Is pay 80 percent the same as 20 percent off?
Same amount, opposite phrasing. One describes what you pay, the other what you save; both come out to price times 0.8. Convert to one format before doing the arithmetic.
How much does second item 40 percent off really save?
An average of 20 percent over two items. It is only a saving when you needed both; buying a second item just to unlock the discount usually costs more.

loc.title: 며칠 지났는지 정확히 세는 법: 첫날을 1일로 셀까, 0일로 셀까
loc.meta: 며칠 지났는지는 첫날을 어떻게 세느냐에 따라 하루가 달라집니다. 100일 계산과 D-day 계산의 차이, 수능까지 남은 날을 홈 화면에 두는 방법을 정리합니다. CountDaysNow는 지난날·오늘·다가올 날을 정확한 날짜 수로 보여 줍니다.
loc.h1: 며칠 지났는지 세는 법: 100일과 D-day는 규칙이 다릅니다
loc.lead: 사귄 지 100일, 금연한 지 며칠, 수능까지 며칠. 같은 '며칠'인데 세는 규칙이 달라서 하루씩 어긋납니다.
loc.answer: 며칠 지났는지는 오늘 날짜에서 시작일을 빼면 되지만, 한국식 100일은 시작일을 1일로 세기 때문에 그 결과에 1을 더해야 하고, 수능 같은 D-day는 당일이 D-day, 전날이 D-1이라 아무것도 더하지 않습니다.
paras: 며칠 지났는지 셀 때 먼저 정할 것은 첫날이 1일인지 0일인지입니다. 달력 계산은 두 날짜의 차이를 구하므로 시작일 당일은 0일입니다. 그런데 한국에서 100일, 1000일을 셀 때는 사귄 날이나 태어난 날을 1일로 치는 관습이 있어서, 달력 차이에 1을 더해야 흔히 말하는 100일이 됩니다. 이 하루 차이 때문에 기념일을 하루 늦게 챙기는 일이 생깁니다.

반대로 다가올 날을 세는 D-day는 당일이 D-day, 하루 전이 D-1입니다. 수능까지 남은 날을 셀 때는 시험일을 0으로 두고 오늘까지의 차이를 그대로 쓰면 됩니다. 앱을 쓴다면 시작일을 0일로 계산하는지 1일로 계산하는지 한 번만 확인해 두면 되고, 손으로 셀 때는 달마다 다른 일수 때문에 달이 바뀌는 지점에서 틀리기 쉬우니 날짜 계산기를 쓰는 편이 정확합니다.

자주 보는 숫자는 홈 화면에 두는 편이 매일 앱을 여는 것보다 오래갑니다. CountDaysNow는 지난날·오늘·다가올 날을 세 가지 보기로 나누어 정확한 날짜 수를 보여 주고, 날짜를 더하거나 빼고 비교하는 계산기가 있습니다. 홈 화면 위젯은 모든 크기를 지원하고, 잠금화면과 다이내믹 아일랜드에서 남은 날이 실시간으로 이어지며, 7일·3일·1일 전과 당일, 100일에 알려 줍니다.

en.title: How many days since: count from day one or day zero
en.meta: Counting days since a date goes wrong by one depending on whether the first day counts. The difference between anniversary counting and D-day counting, and how to keep the number on the Home Screen. CountDaysNow shows Since, Today and Ahead with exact day counts.
en.h1: How many days since: anniversaries and D-days follow different rules
en.lead: Days since you quit, days since you met, days until the exam. The same word, two counting rules, and a one-day gap between them.
en.answer: Days since equals today's date minus the start date; for 100-day anniversaries counted the Korean way the start day is day one so you add one, while a D-day such as an exam counts the day itself as D-day and the day before as D-1 with nothing added.
paras: Before counting how many days since something happened, decide whether the first day is day one or day zero. Calendar arithmetic gives the difference between two dates, so the start day itself is zero. Many anniversary traditions, including the Korean 100-day and 1,000-day milestones, count the first day as day one, which means adding one to the calendar difference. That single day is why couples and parents sometimes celebrate a milestone a day late.

Counting toward a future date works the other way. The day itself is D-day and the day before is D-1, so for an exam you set the exam date as zero and use the plain calendar difference. If you use an app for both, check once whether it treats the start date as zero or one. Doing it by hand across month boundaries is where mistakes happen, because months have different lengths, so a date calculator is more reliable than counting squares on a calendar.

A number you look at daily belongs on the Home Screen rather than behind an app icon. CountDaysNow keeps past, current and future events in three views, Since, Today and Ahead, with precise day counts and a date calculator for adding, subtracting or comparing dates. Home Screen widgets come in every size, the countdown continues live on the Lock Screen and in the Dynamic Island, and alerts arrive 7, 3 and 1 day before, on the day and at day 100. Widgets are available from the start.

loc.title: Lärmmessgerät im iPhone: Lautstärke messen und dB-Werte richtig einordnen
loc.meta: Wann reicht das iPhone als Lärmmessgerät, was bedeuten 40, 60 und 85 dB, und wo ein Smartphone-Mikrofon an seine Grenzen kommt. dB Halo zeigt den Pegel mit Minimum, Mittelwert, Maximum und Spitze, A-, C- oder Z-Bewertung und Kalibrierungsprofilen.
loc.h1: Lärmmessgerät im iPhone: Was die dB-Zahl aussagt und wo sie endet
loc.lead: Ob Nachbarn, Büro oder Konzert: Die Zahl auf dem Display ist nur so viel wert, wie Sie über Bewertung, Mittelwert und Mikrofon wissen.
loc.answer: Ein iPhone taugt als Lärmmessgerät für Orientierungswerte zwischen etwa 30 und 100 dB, wenn Sie A-Bewertung, den Mittelwert statt der Spitze und eine Kalibrierung gegen ein Referenzgerät nutzen; für Nachweise oder Arbeitsschutz braucht es ein zertifiziertes Messgerät.
paras: Ein Lärmmessgerät gibt den Schalldruck in Dezibel an, und die Skala ist logarithmisch: Plus 10 dB wird ungefähr als doppelt so laut empfunden, plus 3 dB bedeutet bereits die doppelte Schallenergie. Zur Einordnung: Ein ruhiges Schlafzimmer liegt um 30 dB, eine normale Wohnung tagsüber bei 40 bis 50, ein Gespräch bei etwa 60, dichter Straßenverkehr bei 70 bis 80, ein Konzert vor der Bühne über 100. Entscheidend ist nicht die einzelne Spitze, sondern der Mittelwert über die Zeit, die Sie dem Lärm ausgesetzt sind.

Die zweite Frage ist die Bewertung. A-Bewertung bildet das menschliche Gehör nach und wird im Arbeitsschutz und bei Lärmrichtwerten verwendet; C-Bewertung behält tiefe Frequenzen und ist bei Bässen oder Maschinenbrummen aussagekräftiger; Z ist unbewertet. Vergleichen Sie Ihre Zahl nur mit Grenzwerten derselben Bewertung. In Deutschland gilt im Arbeitsschutz ab 80 dB(A) der untere und ab 85 dB(A) der obere Auslösewert, jeweils als Tages-Mittelwert, und bei Nachbarschaftslärm zählen Richtwerte nach Gebietsart und Tageszeit.

Ein Smartphone-Mikrofon ist für Sprache gebaut, nicht für Messungen. Es komprimiert bei sehr hohen Pegeln, zeigt in stillen Räumen eher sein Eigenrauschen und ist ab Werk nicht kalibriert. Behandeln Sie die Werte deshalb als Schätzung und kalibrieren Sie gegen ein Referenzgerät, wenn Sie mehr als Orientierung wollen. dB Halo zeigt den aktuellen Pegel im Halo samt Minimum, Mittelwert, Maximum und Spitze, lässt A-, C- oder Z-Bewertung wählen, nimmt ein externes Mikrofon an und speichert mehrere Kalibrierungsprofile; die App weist selbst darauf hin, dass ihre Messwerte Schätzungen sind und sie kein zertifizierter Schallpegelmesser ist.

en.title: Using an iPhone as a noise meter: what the dB values mean and where it stops
en.meta: When an iPhone is good enough as a noise meter, what 40, 60 and 85 dB mean, and where a phone microphone hits its limits. dB Halo shows the live level with minimum, average, maximum and peak, A, C or Z weighting and calibration profiles.
en.h1: iPhone as a noise meter: what the dB number tells you and where it ends
en.lead: Neighbours, office or concert: the number on the screen is only as good as what you know about weighting, averages and the microphone.
en.answer: An iPhone works as a noise meter for orientation between roughly 30 and 100 dB if you use A weighting, read the average rather than the peak and calibrate against a reference meter; for evidence or occupational safety you need a certified instrument.
paras: A noise meter reports sound pressure in decibels, and the scale is logarithmic: an extra 10 dB is perceived as roughly twice as loud, and an extra 3 dB already means double the sound energy. For reference, a quiet bedroom sits around 30 dB, a normal home in the daytime at 40 to 50, conversation at about 60, heavy traffic at 70 to 80, and a concert near the stage above 100. What matters is not the single spike but the average over the time you are exposed.

The second question is weighting. A weighting mimics human hearing and is what occupational limits and residential guidelines use; C weighting keeps low frequencies and says more about bass or machinery hum; Z is unweighted. Only compare your reading with limits that use the same weighting. In most occupational rules the action levels sit around 80 and 85 dB(A) as a daily average, while neighbourhood noise is judged against guideline values that depend on the area type and the time of day.

A phone microphone is built for speech, not measurement. It compresses at very high levels, shows mostly its own noise floor in quiet rooms and is not calibrated out of the box. Treat the values as estimates and calibrate against a reference meter if you need more than orientation. dB Halo shows the live level in its Halo ring with minimum, average, maximum and peak, lets you choose A, C or Z weighting, accepts an external microphone and saves multiple calibration profiles, and states itself that its measurements are estimates and that it is not a certified sound level meter.

Für Lesbarkeit zählen drei Dinge. Erstens Kontrast: helle Schrift auf dunklem Grund trägt weiter als schwarz auf weiß. Drittens Ruhe: Ein Name steht besser still, Laufschrift ist für längere Sätze gedacht, etwa für den Ausgang oder den Treffpunkt. en.meta: Paper or screen? An airport pickup sign has to be readable from ten metres: large static type, high contrast, screen turned sideways. LED Moving Text shows one line full screen, with size, colour and speed edited right in the preview.
en.h1: Airport pickup sign: how to make the name readable from ten metres
en.lead: In the arrivals hall your guest has about two seconds to find you. The sign has to carry the name, because your voice will not.
en.answer: An airport pickup sign works when the name is the only line, in large static high-contrast type, held above head height; on an iPhone that means landscape or letters turned ninety degrees, full brightness and a charged battery.
paras: An airport pickup sign has one job: the arriving passenger should recognise their name before they start scanning the hall. So the sign carries only what they will recognise instantly, surname or company, no greeting, no flight number. Fewer characters means bigger type. Paper loses in practice because it creases, turns grey against backlight and gets covered when you wave; a bright screen stays readable in a dim hall and behind the barrier.

Three things decide readability. First, contrast: light type on a dark background carries further than black on white. Second, size: a short name should fill the full width, and if the phone is held upright, letters turned ninety degrees use the full height. Third, stillness: a name reads better static, while scrolling text is for longer lines such as the exit or the meeting point. Set brightness to maximum and switch off auto-lock, or the sign goes dark in the middle of the wait.

You can build such a sign in any notes app, but you lose a borderless full screen, text size by gesture and a quick switch between a static name and a scrolling line. LED Moving Text opens straight onto a live canvas where the preview is the editor: the words, the speed, the size and the colour change the moment you do, one tap takes it full screen, a pinch resizes the letters, and the sideways ninety-degree mode plus still and scrolling motion are part of the free tier.

paras: 底片的「味道」其實是幾個可以拆開的東西：高光偏暖或偏綠、暗部帶一點藍、顆粒粗細、邊角暗角，加上偶爾出現的漏光。套一下就「很復古」的濾鏡，常常是把這些全部一次拉滿，結果整張照片的膚色跟著偏黃或偏綠，人看起來像生病。
比較穩的做法是先選一個基底色調，再分開決定要不要加顆粒和漏光。拍人像時顆粒可以留著，它讓皮膚看起來不像塑膠，但漏光要放在沒有臉的角落。PhotoCream Pro：底片濾鏡·復古修圖 把超過 100 種真實膠片濾鏡和光影色調、顆粒、邊框分成獨立的調整項，而且有即時預覽，拍之前就能看到效果；它是一次性購買，無需訂閱、無廣告，所有編輯都在裝置上完成。
最後一步永遠是放大看臉。底片感的照片可以整體偏色，但眼白不應該變綠、嘴唇不應該變灰。如果需要修皮膚，用頻率分離這種把質地和顏色分開處理的方式，比直接把整張磨平更保得住底片顆粒。

en.h1: Film look on iPhone: tone, grain and skin are three separate jobs
en.lead: Most film filters feel vintage for a second, and then you notice the face has gone green. The filter is rarely the problem; tone, grain and skin got bundled into one slider.
en.answer: A convincing analog look is a colour tone (the mood), grain and light leaks (the texture), and skin that still reads as skin (the limit). Set the tone first, add texture second, then check the face on its own. Done in that order, it does not need a subscription.
paras: Real film has a handful of separable traits: highlights that lean warm or green, shadows with a touch of blue, grain of a certain size, darkened corners and the occasional light leak. One-tap retro presets push all of them at once, which is why the whole frame, face included, drifts yellow or green and people start looking unwell.

The steadier approach is to pick a base tone, then decide on grain and light leaks separately. For portraits keep the grain, it stops skin looking like plastic, but keep leaks in corners away from the face. PhotoCream Pro: Film Filters gives you 100+ hand-tuned looks with grain, halation, light leaks and vignette as separate controls, full curves, HSL and split toning, and a live preview so you see the exact look before you shoot. It is free to download with a single one-time unlock, no subscription, no ads, and everything is processed on the device.

The last step is always zooming into the face. A film look can shift the whole image, but the whites of the eyes should not go green and lips should not go grey. If skin needs smoothing, use a frequency-separation method that treats texture and colour separately; it keeps the film grain where flattening the whole frame would erase it.

en.lead: Posters in the station, the slip on a parcel, a payment notice in the mailbox. A QR code jumps straight to a page, and tapping a link you never saw is the most common phishing entry point today.
en.answer: Make the scanner show and not open. Then check three things: is it https, is the host the company you expect rather than a lookalike, and is there a long string of odd parameters after the path. Open only if all three pass; one failure means leave it.

Stickers pasted over a printed poster, or an extra label on a pickup slip, are where this shows up most.

Seeing the whole payload needs a scanner that does not run the action automatically. QR Code Halo: Scan & Create lets you turn off Run action after scanning in Settings and is built around Inspect, Decide, Act: it parses the complete payload on the device into scheme, host, path, query and fragment, applies deterministic rules that return Safe, Caution or Blocked with transparent findings, and fails closed when parsing is uncertain. No network reputation lookup, no fuzzy score. Three successful scans are included per device; the optional Lifetime Pro is a single purchase with no subscription.

Payment codes deserve one extra check: compare the host against the company name and address printed on the slip, not against how polished the page looks. If the code decodes to plain text, a phone number or Wi-Fi details rather than a URL, read the whole content before acting on it.

en.title: Does brown noise help you sleep, and how to play it offline all night | Sereno: Sleep Sounds
en.meta: Brown noise is low-frequency and softer than white noise. For all-night play: no loops, offline, fade-out timer. Sereno: Sleep Sounds, one-time purchase.
en.h1: Brown noise: why it is easier on the ears and how to run it all night
en.lead: A roommate gaming at 2 a.m., renovation next door, a room facing the road. Plenty of people try white noise, find it harsh and give up. Switching to brown noise changes the experience.
en.answer: Brown noise concentrates its energy in the low end, like a distant waterfall or an aircraft cabin, far gentler than the hiss of white noise and more natural at masking voices and footsteps. For a full night the priorities are sound that never loops, playback that works offline, a timer that fades out, and no interruption when the screen locks.
paras: White, pink and brown noise differ in how energy is spread across frequencies: white is equal everywhere and sounds sharp; pink trims the highs; brown trims them most, leaving a low rumble. Voices and keyboard clicks sit in the mid range, and a bed of low-frequency brown noise pushes them into the distance. It does not remove the noise; it stops sudden sounds from grabbing your attention.

Two things ruin an all-night session: loop seams and a dropped connection. A looping audio file has a seam every few minutes that eventually wakes you, and a streamed sound stops the moment the dorm Wi-Fi drops. Sereno: Sleep Sounds generates its sounds live on the device, so nothing repeats and it works fully offline; you can layer brown noise under a fan or rain and set the volume and EQ of each track, the sleep timer fades out softly instead of cutting off, and it supports background playback with lock-screen controls. It is a one-time purchase with no subscription and no ads.

Set the volume to just cover the loudest sound in the room, not louder. For focus during the day go a notch quieter than for sleep; too loud is tiring. If you play through a Bluetooth speaker or earbuds all night, check the battery will last first.

loc.h1: 語音轉文字筆記：錄下來的話，怎麼變成之後找得到的文字
loc.lead: 錄音最大的問題不是錄不到，是錄完沒有人會回頭聽。把聲音變成文字，筆記才真正開始。
loc.answer: 錄音只有轉成文字才找得回來：在 iPhone 上直接錄、直接轉成摘要與重點，再匯出成文字或 Markdown 放進你平常的筆記工具，之後用關鍵字就搜得到。Sono Note 整個流程都在裝置上完成，不需要帳號。
paras: 先想清楚這段錄音要拿來做什麼。一堂三小時的課、一場客戶會議、走路時冒出來的一個想法，三種錄音需要的「文字」完全不同：課堂要的是重點和可以搜尋的內容，會議要的是行動項目和誰負責，走路時的想法只需要一段乾淨的句子。先決定你要的是哪一種，否則最後只會得到一堆沒人想讀的原始文字。
第二步是把轉錄和整理放在同一個動作裡。Sono Note 的做法是錄完直接交給你一份完成的筆記：摘要、重點、行動項目，還有一封可以直接寄出的後續郵件；原始錄音留在筆記裡隨時可以重播，不用再從頭聽一次。它有課堂、客戶電話、面試、就醫、創意等現成範本，全部在 iPhone 上處理，沒有帳號、飛航模式也能用，捷運進隧道收訊斷掉也不會中斷。
第三步是讓文字真的找得到。轉好的筆記用文字或 Markdown 匯出，放進你平常搜尋的地方——備忘錄、公司的雲端硬碟都可以——下週要找「那次說到的截止日」時，搜關鍵字就跳出來。免費可以每天錄 3 則、每則最多 3 分鐘，先用這個額度試試自己的講話習慣轉出來準不準；要更長的錄音與 PDF 匯出，專業版可以一次性永久解鎖，沒有訂閱。
