en.title: Taking a toddler out in Thailand: which days, what to wear
en.meta: Heat, rain or PM2.5: three numbers decide. Feels-like over 35, go early; rain over 60%, change plans; PM2.5 over 37.5, cut short. Lumi Weather, free to start.
en.h1: Which days to take a toddler outside, and what to dress them in for heat, rain and dust
en.lead: In Thailand the problem is not cold. It is heat, rain and dust, and all three can change within the same day, so the temperature at wake-up time is the wrong number to decide on.
en.answer: Check three numbers before leaving: feels-like temperature (above 35, go before 9 am or after 4 pm), hourly rain chance (above 60% for your hour, pick somewhere indoors) and PM2.5 (above 37.5, shorten the outing; above 75, stay home). Then dress for whichever of the three is the day's problem.
paras: On hot days the number that matters is the feels-like temperature, not the headline figure. Thai humidity turns 33 degrees into 38 to 40 with ease, and toddlers shed heat more slowly than adults. Above a feels-like of 35, keep outdoor play to before 9 am or after 4 pm, 30 to 45 minutes at a time. Dress in thin, light-coloured cotton, short or no sleeves, a wide-brimmed hat, and carry one spare shirt for when the first one is soaked.

In the rainy season read the hourly rain chance, not the daily one. Rain here tends to arrive between three and six in the afternoon, so mornings are often still fine. If the chance for your hour is above 60%, swap to a mall or an indoor playground, and pack a pull-on raincoat (umbrellas rarely work with toddlers) plus spare socks. In dust season check hourly PM2.5 from the station nearest home; values usually peak from before dawn to late morning and ease in the afternoon. Above 37.5 micrograms, shorten the outing and keep away from main roads; above 75, stay in with the windows closed and do not wait for symptoms.

If the morning needs three apps, soon none of them gets opened. Lumi Weather folds feels-like temperature, rain, wind and UV into one outing score weighted for your child's age, points to the gentlest window of the day, and builds a checklist of clothes and things to pack. Dust still needs the source you already use. No ads, no third-party tracking.
look: Feels-like temperature for the hour you will be out, not the wake-up reading
Hourly rain chance for the afternoon if the plan runs late
Hourly PM2.5 from the station near home, not the daily average
UV index if you will be out between 10 am and 3 pm
Whether the destination has shade or air conditioning to retreat to
steps: The night before, open tomorrow's hourly forecast and pick a two-hour window with feels-like under 33 and rain chance under 40%.
In the morning recheck PM2.5. Above 37.5, halve the outing; above 75, cancel and play indoors.
Dress for the day's problem: heat means thin light cotton and a brimmed hat, rain means a pull-on raincoat and quick-dry shoes, a mall means a thin long sleeve for the air conditioning.
Pack before lifting the child into the car: one spare shirt, water, a cooling towel, child sunscreen and a bag for wet clothes.
While playing, touch the back of the neck every 20 minutes. Sweaty or flushed means ten minutes in the shade and a drink, before any whining starts.

PM2.5 is above 37.5. Can we go out if the child wears a mask?

loc.title: Was ziehe ich dem Kind bei wie viel Grad an? Zwiebelprinzip
loc.meta: Von über 25 Grad bis unter null: Schichten-Tabelle fürs Kleinkind nach gefühlter Temperatur, mit Nackenprobe und Windregel. Lumi Wetter: kostenlos zum Start.
loc.h1: Was ziehe ich dem Kind bei X Grad an? Das Zwiebelprinzip in Temperaturstufen
loc.lead: Die Zahl auf dem Thermometer sagt wenig. Bei 10 Grad mit Wind und Nieselregen friert ein Kind schneller als bei 3 Grad in der Sonne. Entscheidend sind die gefühlte Temperatur und die Zahl der Schichten.
loc.answer: Faustregel: über 25 Grad eine Schicht, 15 bis 25 Grad zwei, 5 bis 15 Grad drei, unter 5 Grad drei bis vier Schichten plus Mütze und Handschuhe. Gerechnet wird mit der gefühlten Temperatur, nicht mit der Lufttemperatur, und die Nackenprobe nach zehn Minuten entscheidet, ob eine Schicht wieder weg kommt.
paras: Das Zwiebelprinzip funktioniert nur, wenn jede Schicht eine Aufgabe hat: Die innere Schicht (Body oder Unterhemd aus Baumwolle oder Wolle-Seide) nimmt Schweiß auf, die mittlere (Pulli, Fleece, Strickjacke) wärmt, die äußere (Jacke, Regenhose, Schneeanzug) hält Wind und Nässe ab. Zwei dünne Schichten wärmen besser als eine dicke, weil die Luft dazwischen isoliert, und unterwegs lässt sich eine ausziehen, ohne dass das Kind plötzlich im T-Shirt steht.

Die Stufen für ein Kleinkind, das sich selbst bewegt: über 25 Grad kurze Kleidung, Sonnenhut, am Wasser ein UV-Shirt. 20 bis 25 Grad ein dünnes Langarmshirt oder T-Shirt, dünne Jacke im Buggy. 15 bis 20 Grad Langarm plus leichte Jacke oder Weste. 10 bis 15 Grad Body, Pulli, Übergangsjacke, bei Wind eine dünne Mütze. 5 bis 10 Grad Unterhemd, Pulli, Winterjacke, Mütze, Handschuhe. 0 bis 5 Grad Funktionsunterwäsche, Fleece, Winterjacke oder Schneeanzug, Schal. Unter 0 Grad Schneeanzug, Wollsocken, im Buggy ein Fußsack, und nach 30 bis 45 Minuten wieder rein. Babys, die getragen werden oder liegen, bekommen eine Schicht mehr als die Tabelle, Kinder, die rennen, eher eine weniger.

Der Fehler passiert selten bei der Tabelle, sondern beim Blick aufs Thermometer: Wind, Nässe und fehlende Sonne ziehen mehrere Grad ab. Lumi Wetter rechnet mit gefühlter Temperatur, UV, Regenwahrscheinlichkeit und Wind, gewichtet nach dem Alter des Kindes, zeigt eine Ausflugspunktzahl mit Erklärung für jeden Punkt und eine Outfit-Checkliste, die sich mit dem Wetter und dem Alter ändert. Die Heute-Ansicht ist kostenlos, ohne Werbung und ohne Konto.

Zehn Minuten nach dem Rausgehen die Nackenprobe: warm und trocken ist richtig, feucht heißt eine Schicht weg, kühl heißt Mütze oder Jacke dazu. Hände und Füße fühlen sich oft kälter an, als dem Kind ist.

en.title: What to dress a child in at X degrees: layers by temperature
en.meta: From above 25 degrees to below zero: a toddler layering chart built on feels-like temperature, with the neck test and a wind rule. Lumi Weather is free to start.
en.h1: What to put on a child at X degrees: the layering principle in temperature bands
en.lead: The thermometer tells you little. A child gets cold faster at 10 degrees with wind and drizzle than at 3 degrees in the sun. What matters is the feels-like temperature and the number of layers.
en.answer: Rule of thumb: above 25 degrees one layer, 15 to 25 two, 5 to 15 three, below 5 three to four layers plus hat and gloves. Work from the feels-like temperature, not the air temperature, and let the neck test after ten minutes decide whether a layer comes off.
paras: Layering only works when each layer has a job: the inner layer (a cotton or wool-silk bodysuit or vest) takes up sweat, the middle (jumper, fleece, cardigan) warms, the outer (jacket, rain trousers, snowsuit) keeps out wind and wet. Two thin layers are warmer than one thick one because the air between them insulates, and one can come off on the way without leaving the child in a T-shirt.

The bands for a toddler who moves on their own: above 25 degrees, shorts and a sun hat, a UV shirt near water. 20 to 25, a thin long sleeve or T-shirt with a light jacket in the buggy. 15 to 20, long sleeve plus a light jacket or gilet. 10 to 15, bodysuit, jumper, transitional jacket, a thin hat if windy. 5 to 10, vest, jumper, winter coat, hat, gloves. 0 to 5, thermal base layer, fleece, winter coat or snowsuit, scarf. Below 0, snowsuit, wool socks, a footmuff in the buggy, and back inside after 30 to 45 minutes. Babies who are carried or lying down get one layer more than the chart; children who run get one less.

The mistake is rarely the chart. It is reading the thermometer: wind, wet and missing sun take several degrees off. Lumi Weather works from feels-like temperature, UV, rain chance and wind, weighted for the child's age, and shows an outing score with every point explained plus an outfit checklist that changes with the weather and the child's age. The Today view is free, with no ads and no account.

The removed layer goes in the buggy or backpack, not tied around the child; it is needed again on the way home as evening cools.

As a base, yes, but with one extra layer, because babies do not move and hold temperature less well. In a footmuff or carrier the carrier counts as a layer, so no thick coat underneath.

Damp neck, red face, fussing for no reason. Take the middle layer off at once and offer a drink. Cold hands on their own are not a sign of being cold.

loc.title: 带娃出门怎么按温度穿衣？分层法温度对照表
loc.meta: 别只看气温，看体感温度：25度以上单层，15到25度两层，5到15度三层，5度以下三层加帽子手套；体感超过35度、空气质量指数超过150或有雷雨，就待在家。Lumi 天气星球给出外出指数和穿搭清单，免费开始。
loc.h1: 带娃出门按温度穿衣：分层法对照表，以及哪些天该直接待在家
loc.lead: 孩子着凉往往不是穿少了，而是穿多了出汗再被风吹。按体感温度分层，比按气温一件件加衣更可靠。
loc.answer: 按体感温度分层：25度以上一层，15到25度两层，5到15度三层，5度以下三层加帽子、手套、围巾；出门十分钟摸后颈，温热干爽就对了。体感超过35度、空气质量指数超过150、有雷雨或6级以上大风，当天就待在家。
paras: 分层法的关键是每层各管一件事：内层贴身排汗，选棉或莫代尔，别用化纤；中层保暖，用抓绒、毛衣或薄羽绒内胆；外层挡风防水，用冲锋衣、风衣或雨衣。两件薄的比一件厚的暖，因为中间夹着空气，而且进商场、上地铁时能脱一件，不会一下子从棉服变成单衣。
对照表按会自己跑动的幼儿算：28度以上短袖短裤加遮阳帽；23到28度单层长袖或短袖，推车里备薄外套；18到23度长袖加薄外套或马甲；12到18度内层加毛衣加防风外套，有风戴薄帽；5到12度内层、毛衣、厚外套，加帽子手套；0到5度保暖内衣、抓绒、羽绒服或棉服，加围巾；0度以下再加厚袜子、推车用脚套，每次在外不超过30到45分钟。被抱着或躺在推车里的宝宝比表上多穿一层，跑跳不停的大孩子可以少一层。
多数穿错不是表不对，而是只看了气温：风、湿度和没太阳都会让体感低好几度。Lumi 天气星球把体感温度、降雨、风和紫外线合成一个按孩子年龄给的外出指数，找出一天里较舒服的出门时段，自动生成穿搭与物品清单，Lumi 还会随天气换装，孩子自己也看得懂。无广告、无第三方追踪。

风力：5级以上要把防风层穿在外面，或多加一层
未来一小时的降水概率：淋湿比冷更快带走体温
孩子是自己走，还是坐推车、在背带里
空气质量指数：超过100缩短时间，超过150不出门

按对照表摆出三层：内层排汗、中层保暖、外层挡风防水。
坐推车、背带的多加一层；会跑会爬的减一层。
出门十分钟摸后颈：温热干爽刚好，潮湿就脱一层，发凉就加帽子或外套。手脚凉不算冷。
脱下来的那层放进推车或背包，别系在孩子身上；傍晚回程温度会往下掉，到时再穿回去。

这个区间外层决定一切：有风或下雨，就按低一档的温度穿

只能当粗略参考。它把每件衣服的保暖值固定了，却没算风、湿度和孩子的活动量。按体感温度分层，再用后颈判断，比把各件衣服的数字加起来更准。

en.title: Layering kids' clothes by temperature, and when to stay in
en.meta: Layer kids' clothes by feels-like temperature: one layer above 25, two at 15 to 25, three at 5 to 15. Storms or AQI over 150: stay in. Lumi Weather is free to start.
en.h1: Dressing a child by temperature with layers, and the days to stay home instead
en.lead: Children usually catch a chill not from too few clothes but from too many: they sweat, then the wind hits. Layering by feels-like temperature beats piling on clothes by the thermometer.
en.answer: Layer by feels-like temperature: one layer above 25 degrees, two from 15 to 25, three from 5 to 15, three plus hat, gloves and scarf below 5. Ten minutes after going out, touch the back of the neck: warm and dry is right. Feels-like above 35, AQI above 150, thunderstorms or strong wind mean a day at home.
paras: The point of layering is that each layer has one job. The inner layer wicks sweat, so cotton or modal rather than synthetics. The middle layer warms: fleece, a jumper or a thin down liner. The outer layer blocks wind and rain: a shell, windbreaker or raincoat. Two thin layers beat one thick one because the air between them insulates, and one can come off in a mall or on the metro without going straight from padded coat to T-shirt.

The chart assumes a toddler who runs around. Above 28 degrees, short sleeves and shorts with a sun hat. 23 to 28, one long- or short-sleeved layer with a light jacket in the buggy. 18 to 23, long sleeve plus light jacket or gilet. 12 to 18, base layer, jumper and windproof jacket, a thin hat if windy. 5 to 12, base layer, jumper, heavy coat, hat and gloves. 0 to 5, thermal underwear, fleece, down or padded coat, scarf. Below 0, add thick socks and a buggy footmuff, and keep each outing under 30 to 45 minutes. A baby who is carried or lying in the buggy gets one layer more than the chart; a bigger child who never stops moving can take one off.

Most mistakes are not the chart, they are reading only the air temperature: wind, humidity and a missing sun pull the feels-like down several degrees. Lumi Weather blends feels-like temperature, rain, wind and UV into one outing score set for your child's age, finds the gentler window of the day to go out, and builds an outfit and packing list automatically. Lumi the character changes clothes with the weather, so the child understands too. No ads, no third-party tracking.

faq: Does the old 26-degree clothing rule still work?

Only as a rough guide. It assigns a fixed warmth value to each garment and ignores wind, humidity and how much the child moves. Layering by feels-like temperature and checking the neck is more reliable than adding up garment numbers.
Which days should we simply stay home?
Feels-like above 35 or below minus 10, AQI above 150, thunderstorm or heavy-rain warnings, and wind at force 6 or more. Those days are not solved by dressing right; switch to indoor play.

loc.meta: マーカーの黒塗りは明るさを上げると透け、PDF の黒い四角は下の文字が残ります。「不透明で上書き→別ファイルで書き出し→開き直して確認」の手順を解説。Mask My File は無料で始められ、買い切りです。
loc.h1: 書類やスクショを送る前に個人情報を隠す正しい手順（黒塗りで消えていないケース）
loc.lead: 黒く塗ったはずの住所や口座番号が、受け取った側で読めてしまう事故は珍しくありません。原因は塗り方の雑さではなく、「見た目を変えただけでデータが残っている」ことです。
loc.answer: 隠したい部分を不透明な塗りつぶしで画素ごと上書きし、元とは別の新しいファイルとして書き出し、その書き出したファイルを開き直して「本当に消えたか」を確認してから送る——この三段階を守れば、黒塗りが透ける・はがれる事故は防げます。
paras: 黒塗りが「消えていない」原因は、ほぼ三つに絞れます。マーカーの不透明度が 100 未満で、受け取った側が明るさやコントラストを上げると下の文字が浮かぶ。PDF の上に黒い四角を置いただけで、本文のテキストが残っていて選択やコピー、検索で読める。写真アプリで加工しても元画像が残っていて「元に戻す」で戻せる——いずれも見た目だけが変わり、データは残ったままです。

だから手順は「上書き→別ファイル→検証」の順になります。隠す部分は半透明のマーカーではなく不透明な塗りつぶしで画素ごと置き換え、PDF なら注釈を重ねるのではなく中身のテキストごと消す処理を選びます。書き出しは必ず元と別の新しいファイルにして、送るのはそのファイルだけにします。送信前に書き出したファイルを開き直し、画像なら明るさを上げて透けないか、PDF ならテキスト選択と検索で何も拾えないかを確かめます。

en.title: Hide personal info on documents so the blackout cannot be undone

en.h1: The right order for hiding personal info on documents and screenshots (when the blackout did not actually erase anything)
en.lead: An address or account number you blacked out being readable on the other end is a common accident. The cause is rarely sloppy painting; it is that only the appearance changed and the data stayed.
en.answer: Overwrite the area pixel by pixel with an opaque fill, export it as a new file separate from the original, then reopen that exported file and confirm the data is really gone before you send it. Keep those three stages in that order and a blackout that lifts or peels off stops happening.
paras: A blackout that is not really gone comes down to three causes. A highlighter whose opacity is under 100, so raising brightness or contrast on the receiving end brings the text back. A black rectangle placed on top of a PDF, with the body text still underneath and selectable, copyable and searchable. An edit in the Photos app that keeps the original and can be reverted with one tap. In every case the look changed and the data did not.

That is why the order is overwrite, new file, verify. Replace the pixels with an opaque fill rather than a translucent marker, and on a PDF choose a process that removes the underlying text rather than stacking an annotation on it. Always export to a new file separate from the original, and send only that file. Before sending, reopen the export: on an image, push brightness up and check nothing shows through; on a PDF, try selecting and searching for the hidden text.

Reopening and checking by hand every time is the tedious part, and skipping it is where accidents happen. Mask My File permanently blacks out or removes the regions you select on images and PDFs, then reopens the exported file and verifies it before showing Private Ready. Everything is processed on the device and originals are never overwritten. Free to start.

loc.title: Como tarjar PDF no iPhone de verdade (não só uma caixa preta)
loc.meta: A caixa preta da Marcação fica por cima: o CPF ainda pode ser selecionado e buscado. Remova o conteúdo, exporte e teste antes de enviar. Mask My File é grátis.
loc.h1: Como tarjar um PDF no iPhone de verdade, e não só desenhar uma caixa preta por cima
loc.lead: Você cobre o CPF com um retângulo preto, manda o comprovante pela imobiliária e, do outro lado, basta segurar o dedo sobre a tarja para o número aparecer. A caixa escondeu da sua tela, não do arquivo.
loc.answer: Tarjar de verdade é remover o conteúdo daquela área do PDF, salvar como um arquivo novo e depois reabrir esse arquivo para testar se o texto ainda pode ser selecionado ou encontrado na busca. Se a busca acha o número, você só desenhou por cima.
paras: Um PDF tem camadas. O que a Marcação do iPhone faz é adicionar uma anotação, um retângulo, por cima da página; o texto original continua lá embaixo, intacto. Quem recebe pode selecionar o trecho, copiar e colar em uma nota, buscar pelo número ou simplesmente apagar a anotação em qualquer editor. Com extrato bancário, holerite, RG e comprovante de residência isso acontece todo dia, e o remetente nem fica sabendo.

O caminho certo tem três partes. Primeiro, a ferramenta precisa remover o conteúdo da região, não cobrir: depois do processo, não pode haver texto nem imagem naquele retângulo. Segundo, o resultado sai como arquivo novo, com outro nome, e o original fica guardado separado. Terceiro, você reabre o arquivo novo e testa: segura o dedo sobre a tarja para ver se seleciona algo e usa a busca com um pedaço do CPF ou do endereço. Se não acha nada, pode enviar.

O passo do teste é o que mais se pula, porque dá trabalho fazer página por página em um extrato de dez folhas. O Mask My File foi feito em volta dele: você marca as áreas no PDF página a página, com zoom de até 5×, ele tarja em definitivo e reabre o arquivo exportado para verificar antes de mostrar o selo Private Ready. Tudo é processado no aparelho, o original nunca é sobrescrito, e dá para começar de graça.

en.title: Redact a PDF on iPhone for real, not just a black box on top

en.h1: How to redact a PDF on iPhone for real, not just draw a black box over it
en.lead: You cover the ID number with a black rectangle, send the statement to the letting agent, and on their end a long press on the box brings the number back. The box hid it from your screen, not from the file.
en.answer: Real redaction removes the content from that area of the PDF, saves the result as a new file, and then reopens that file to test whether the text can still be selected or found by search. If search finds the number, you only drew over it.
paras: A PDF has layers. What Markup on iPhone does is add an annotation, a rectangle, above the page; the original text stays underneath, untouched. The recipient can select the passage, copy it into a note, search for the number, or simply delete the annotation in any editor. This happens every day with bank statements, pay slips, ID scans and proof of address, and the sender never finds out.

The right way has three parts. First, the tool has to remove the content from the region rather than cover it: after processing, there should be no text and no image inside that rectangle. Second, the result goes out as a new file with a different name, and the original stays stored separately. Third, you reopen the new file and test it: long-press on the redaction to see whether anything gets selected, and search for a piece of the ID number or address. If nothing turns up, it is safe to send.

The testing step is the one most often skipped, because doing it page by page on a ten-page statement is tedious. Mask My File is built around it: you mark areas page by page with up to 5× zoom, it redacts them permanently, then reopens the exported file and verifies it before showing Private Ready. Everything runs on the device, the original is never overwritten, and it is free to start.

loc.title: Как замазать данные на документе, чтобы их нельзя было восстановить
loc.meta: Маркер просвечивает при подъёме яркости, а чёрный прямоугольник в PDF не трогает текст под собой. Как закрасить навсегда и проверить. Mask My File — бесплатный старт.
loc.h1: Как замазать личные данные на документе перед отправкой, чтобы их нельзя было восстановить
loc.lead: Замазанный номер паспорта на скриншоте часто читается на другой стороне: достаточно поднять яркость или выделить текст в PDF. Проблема не в аккуратности, а в том, что менялся только вид, а данные оставались.
loc.answer: Невосстановимо — это когда пиксели области заменены сплошной непрозрачной заливкой, в PDF удалён сам текст, а не наложен прямоугольник, результат сохранён отдельным новым файлом, и вы открыли этот файл заново и проверили его перед отправкой.
paras: Три способа замазать, которые восстанавливаются. Маркер из стандартной разметки: его непрозрачность ниже 100, и при подъёме яркости и контраста буквы проступают. Слабое размытие или мелкая мозаика: цифры номера паспорта восстанавливают по остаточным контурам, тем более что сам формат номера известен. Чёрный прямоугольник поверх PDF: это аннотация, текст под ней остаётся, его можно выделить, скопировать, найти поиском или просто удалить аннотацию в любом редакторе.

Поэтому порядок такой: заменить, сохранить отдельно, проверить. Область закрашивается сплошной непрозрачной заливкой, которая заменяет пиксели, а не ложится слоем сверху; в PDF выбирается удаление содержимого, а не рисование. Результат сохраняется новым файлом с другим именем, оригинал остаётся отдельно и никуда не отправляется. Потом новый файл открывают заново: на картинке поднимают яркость, в PDF пробуют выделить текст под заливкой и ищут поиском кусок номера. Если ничего не находится, можно отправлять.

Шаг с проверкой чаще всего пропускают, потому что делать его вручную на каждой странице долго. Mask My File построен вокруг него: вы выделяете области на изображении или в PDF, приложение закрашивает их навсегда или удаляет, затем заново открывает экспортированный файл и проверяет его, и только после этого показывает Private Ready. Всё обрабатывается на устройстве, оригинал никогда не перезаписывается. Начать можно бесплатно.

So the order is replace, save separately, verify. The area is painted with a solid opaque fill that replaces the pixels rather than sitting on top as a layer; in a PDF, the content is removed rather than drawn over. The result is saved as a new file under a different name, and the original stays separate and is never sent. Then the new file is reopened: raise brightness on an image, try selecting text under the fill in a PDF, and search for part of the number. If nothing turns up, it can go out.

The verification step is the one most people skip because doing it by hand on every page takes time. Everything is processed on the device, and the original is never overwritten. Free to start.

For one or two pages, yes: a screenshot is a new image and the annotation becomes pixels. But quality drops, it takes long on a lengthy document, and the screenshot can carry device metadata. For a statement or a contract, redact the PDF itself.
How do I check the data under the fill is really deleted?
Reopen the exported file, long-press the painted area and see whether anything gets selected. Then search for part of the number. If nothing is found, the content was removed.
Is Mask My File a subscription?
No. It is free to start, and one purchase unlocks verified outputs and batch processing for good. No subscription, no ads and no account.

loc.h1: 待辦清單一直沒做完怎麼辦：每天 5 件、時間盒、週末清理
loc.lead: 清單做不完，通常不是做太慢，而是清單一開始就裝了做不完的量。先把量壓下來，完成率才會回來。
loc.answer: 每天早上只留 5 件、每件標一個 25 或 50 分鐘的時間盒、週日固定 15 分鐘把沒動的項目刪掉或縮小——三件事一起做，清單一週內就會開始清空。
paras: 多數人的待辦清單同時裝了三種東西：今天一定要做的、這週想做的、以及「總有一天」的念頭。三種混在一起，眼睛每次掃過去都先看到做不到的那幾件，就會覺得整份清單在責備你，然後乾脆不開。做法是把清單拆成「今天」和「之後」兩份，今天這份不超過 5 件，剩下全部丟到之後。
第二步是給每件事一個時間盒。「寫報告」這種項目會無限膨脹，「寫報告：先列大綱，25 分鐘」就會結束。上班族可以用 25 分鐘配一節會議空檔，學生用 50 分鐘配一節課的長度；時間到就停，沒做完的部分變成明天的第一件，不要當天硬撐。
第三步是週末清理：每週日花 15 分鐘看「之後」清單，兩週沒動的直接刪掉，或縮小成一個 25 分鐘能做完的步驟。清單維持在看一眼就看得完的長度，才會每天願意打開。Mochi 就是為這種短清單設計的：寫下任務、點小圓圈打勾、設提醒，主畫面小工具讓今天的 5 件一直看得到。免費開始，沒有廣告。

先停下來，把剩下的部分寫成一個新項目，放進明天的第一件。連續三天都做不完同一件，代表它太大，要再拆。

不是。免費開始、沒有廣告；進階版是 App 內購買一次解鎖，不是每月扣款。

en.title: To-do list never finished? Five a day, time boxes, weekend reset
en.meta: Unfinished lists mix today's work with someday ideas. Keep five a day, time-box each one, clear the rest on Sunday. Mochi is free to start, no ads.
en.h1: What to do when your to-do list never gets finished: five a day, time boxes, a weekend reset
en.lead: A list that never empties is rarely a speed problem. It was overfilled before the day began, and the completion rate only comes back once the volume comes down.
en.answer: Keep five items for today, give each a 25- or 50-minute time box, and spend a fixed 15 minutes every Sunday deleting or shrinking anything that has not moved. Do all three and the list starts emptying within a week.
paras: Most to-do lists hold three kinds of things at once: what must happen today, what you would like to do this week, and ideas for someday. Mixed together, your eye lands first on the items you cannot do, the whole list starts to feel like a reproach, and you stop opening it. Split it into a today list and a later list. Today holds five at most; everything else goes to later.

Next, give each item a time box. "Write the report" expands forever; "Report: outline only, 25 min" ends. At work, 25 minutes fits the gap between meetings; for students, 50 minutes matches a class period. When the timer ends, stop, and whatever is left becomes tomorrow's first item instead of tonight's overtime.

Last is the weekend reset: 15 minutes on Sunday going through the later list. Anything untouched for two weeks gets deleted or shrunk to one step that fits a 25-minute box. A list you can read in one glance is a list you keep opening. Mochi is built for exactly this kind of short list: write the task, tap the little circle to finish, set a reminder, and keep today's five on your Home Screen with a widget. Free to start, no ads.

steps: Dump everything from notes, sticky pads and your head into the later list. Do not filter yet.
Each morning (or the night before) move five items into today, in order, with the one you keep putting off first.
Write a time box after each: "25 min" or "50 min". Start the timer when you start; when it ends, tick it or send it back to later.
Check once at 4 pm: how many are left? More than two means one moves to tomorrow now, so you do not carry an unfinished list home.
Sunday evening, 15 minutes on the later list: delete what has not moved in two weeks, split anything too big into one 25-minute step.

en.fits: Mochi suits office workers and students who want a list that stays short, visible and satisfying to tick. It is a checklist with reminders, not a project tool; anyone who needs Gantt charts or shared team boards should look elsewhere. The free version has 2 lists of 4 items each and 5 themes; unlimited lists and items plus all 101 themes are a one-time Premium unlock.
faq: What if I finish all five with time to spare?
Pull one more from later, but never pre-load it into today. An early empty list is the point; it makes you open the app tomorrow. Starting with eight is what drives completion down.
The time box ended and the task is half done. Now what?
Stop. Write the remaining part as a new item and make it tomorrow's first. If the same task fails three days running, it is too big and needs splitting again.
Is Mochi a subscription?
No. It is free to start with no ads; Premium is a one-time in-app purchase, not a monthly charge.

loc.h1: 할 일 목록을 꾸준히 쓰는 법, 아침 3분 루틴 하나면 됩니다
loc.lead: 목록을 안 쓰게 되는 날은 "바쁜 날"이 아니라 "쓸 타이밍이 없었던 날"입니다. 타이밍을 고정하면 바쁜 날에도 끊기지 않습니다.
loc.answer: 매일 아침 이미 하는 행동 하나에 붙여서(커피 내리는 동안, 지하철 타자마자) 3분만 씁니다. 1분은 어제 남은 것 지우거나 옮기기, 1분은 오늘 할 일 다섯 개 적기, 1분은 첫 번째 할 일에 알림 걸기. 이 순서를 2주만 지키면 습관이 됩니다.
paras: 할 일 목록이 끊기는 패턴은 거의 똑같습니다. 첫 주는 생각날 때마다 적고, 둘째 주부터 "나중에 정리해야지" 하다가, 셋째 주에는 어제 목록이 그대로 남아 있어서 열기 싫어집니다. 문제는 의지가 아니라 쓰는 시간이 정해져 있지 않다는 것입니다. 생각날 때 쓰는 목록은 바쁜 날 가장 먼저 사라집니다.

그래서 이미 매일 하는 행동 하나에 3분을 붙입니다. 커피 머신 돌아가는 동안, 지하철 자리 잡자마자, 강의실에 앉자마자. 첫 1분은 어제 목록을 봅니다. 끝낸 건 체크, 못 한 건 오늘로 옮기거나 과감히 지웁니다. 둘째 1분은 오늘 할 일을 다섯 개까지만 적고, 셋째 1분은 그중 첫 번째에 알림 시간을 겁니다. 알림이 울리는 순간이 목록을 다시 여는 두 번째 타이밍이 됩니다.

2주 동안은 이 3분 외에는 목록을 꾸미지도, 재정리하지도 않습니다. 매일 같은 3분이 쌓이면 "오늘 뭐 하지"를 고민하는 시간이 사라지고, 목록을 여는 게 아침 루틴의 일부가 됩니다. Mochi는 이 3분에 맞게 가볍습니다. 적고, 작은 동그라미를 탭해 완료하고, 알림을 걸고, 홈 화면 위젯과 Apple Watch로 오늘 목록을 바로 봅니다. 무료로 시작하고 광고가 없습니다.

en.title: How to keep a to-do list going: the three-minute morning routine
en.meta: Lists die without a fixed moment to write them. Same anchor each morning, three minutes: clear yesterday, write five, set one reminder. Mochi is free to start.
en.h1: How to keep using a to-do list: one three-minute morning routine
en.lead: The days you skip the list are not the busy days; they are the days with no slot for it. Fix the slot and busy days stop breaking the streak.
en.answer: Attach three minutes to something you already do every morning, while the coffee brews or as soon as you sit on the train. One minute to tick or move yesterday's leftovers, one to write today's five, one to set a reminder on the first item. Hold that order for two weeks and it becomes a habit.
paras: The way to-do lists fail is nearly always the same. Week one you write whenever something comes to mind, week two you start saying "I'll sort it later", and by week three yesterday's list is still sitting there untouched and opening the app feels bad. The problem is not willpower; it is that writing has no fixed time. A list written "when I think of it" is the first thing dropped on a busy day.

So you bolt three minutes onto an existing daily action: the coffee machine running, the first seat on the train, sitting down in the lecture hall. Minute one is yesterday: tick what got done, move the rest to today or delete it outright. Minute two is today: write up to five items. Minute three is the first item: give it a reminder time, and that alert becomes the second moment of the day the list gets opened.

For two weeks, nothing happens to the list outside those three minutes: no decorating, no reorganising. The same three minutes stacking up removes the "what should I do today" deliberation, and opening the list becomes part of the morning rather than a separate chore. Mochi is light enough for that window: write, tap the little circle to finish, set a reminder, and see today's list on a Home Screen widget or Apple Watch. Free to start, no ads.

steps: Pick one thing you already do every morning: coffee, train, brushing teeth. The moment right after it is your three-minute slot.
Minute one: open yesterday, tick what is done, move or delete what is not. No deliberating.
Minute two: write today's items, five at most. When five are in, the rest go to a later list.
Minute three: set a reminder on the first item for a time you can genuinely start, say 10 am.
Same anchor, same order, for two weeks. Decorating and reorganising wait for one weekend session.

The free version gives 2 lists of 4 items each and 5 themes; unlimited lists and items plus all 101 themes open with a one-time Premium purchase.
faq: What about mornings when I do not even have three minutes?
Do one. Move yesterday's leftovers now and write today's five at lunch instead. What matters is that the app was opened, not that the routine was complete.
Evenings work better for me. Is that fine?
Yes, as long as the evening slot is also attached to an action, such as right after brushing your teeth. What gets fixed is the anchor action, not the clock time.

No. Free to start, no ads, and Premium is a single in-app purchase.

en.title: A cute planner that actually works: weekly study and chores plan
en.meta: A cute planner that lasts keeps study and chores apart, is planned once on Sunday night, and holds three items a day, ticked nightly. Mochi is free to start.
en.h1: A cute planner you actually use: planning study and chores one week at a time
en.lead: Pretty planners that die in two weeks usually died because everything in life landed on one page. Two lists and one planning session a week bring them back.
en.answer: Keep two separate lists, study and chores. Plan the whole week once, 15 minutes on Sunday night, with at most three items per list per day, each written as a subject plus pages, or a chore plus the time you will really do it.
paras: Most students open a planner with good intentions, and the first page ends up holding "biology chapter 4", "laundry", "gift for Mint" and "lose weight" side by side. Nothing says where to start, so decorating the page takes over. The fix is two clearly separate lists, one for study and one for chores, with everything else parked in a later list.

Second, plan once for the whole week rather than every morning. On Sunday night, check the timetable for tests and deadlines, then spread the reading across Monday to Friday, no more than three items a day, each measurable: "maths, exercise 2.3, questions 1–10", not "do maths". Chores work the same way: "laundry, Saturday morning", "bathroom, Wednesday after school", with the real time attached.

Last, there has to be a visible tick every day, because a planner without a tick box becomes an ordinary notebook within a week. Mochi fits this exactly: a study list and a chores list kept apart, tasks with reminders, a little circle to tap when done, a cute theme for each list, and a Home Screen widget that shows today without opening the app. Free to start, no ads.

steps: Create two lists named Study and Chores, with a different theme each so they are told apart at a glance.

Make every item measurable: "physics chapter 3, pages 40–52" or "English, 20 vocabulary words", never "read physics".
Add chores with the real day and time, "laundry, Saturday 9 am", and set a reminder 15 minutes before.
Every evening tick what is done and move anything unfinished to the next day immediately; nothing stays overdue for more than one day.

Cut the chores list to the two that truly matter that week, such as laundry and clearing the desk, and move the rest to next week during Sunday planning. No guilt required.

loc.title: Милый планер для учёбы: как вести, чтобы не бросить через неделю
loc.meta: Планер бросают на второй неделе, когда он становится списком невыполненного. Три правила: план раз в неделю, три дела в день, галочка вечером. Mochi — старт бесплатно.
loc.h1: Как вести милый планер для учёбы, чтобы не бросить через неделю
loc.lead: Планер обычно бросают на восьмой-десятый день. Не из-за лени: просто к этому моменту он превращается из красивой страницы в список невыполненного.
loc.answer: Планируйте один раз в неделю, в воскресенье вечером, ставьте не больше трёх учебных дел в день, каждое с конкретным объёмом, и каждый вечер отмечайте сделанное галочкой. Невыполненное переносите сразу, а не копите.
paras: Первая неделя с новым планером — самая приятная: темы, стикеры, аккуратные записи. Проблема начинается, когда вы записываете «подготовиться к контрольной по химии» и «выучить английский» — дела без конца и края. Их невозможно отметить сделанными, они висят день за днём, и через неделю открывать планер уже не хочется. Правило первое: у каждого дела должен быть объём, например «химия, параграф 12, задачи 1–8» или «английский, 20 слов из юнита 3».

Правило второе — планировать не каждое утро, а раз в неделю. В воскресенье вечером откройте расписание, посмотрите, что сдавать и когда контрольные, и распределите подготовку по дням с понедельника по пятницу. Не больше трёх учебных дел в день. Если на неделе семинар и две контрольные, остальное честно уходит в список «потом», а не в понедельник.

Правило третье — вечерняя галочка. Каждый вечер две минуты: отметить сделанное, невыполненное перенести на завтра первым пунктом или удалить. Планер, в котором нечего отмечать, превращается в блокнот. Mochi для такого формата подходит хорошо: отдельный список для учёбы, напоминания, маленький кружок, который приятно нажать после каждого дела, виджет на экране «Домой», чтобы видеть сегодняшнее без открытия приложения, и темы, чтобы учебный список выглядел так, как вам нравится. Начать можно бесплатно, рекламы нет.

Каждое дело пишите с объёмом: «история, глава 5, с. 80–94», а не «почитать историю».
На первое дело каждого дня поставьте напоминание на то время, когда реально сядете, например 16:00.

faq: Три дела в день — не мало ли перед сессией?
Перед сессией можно поднять до четырёх-пяти, но у каждого всё равно должен быть объём, который закрывается за час. «Повторить весь курс» не отметишь никогда.
Что делать, если дело не сделано третий день подряд?
Не переносить снова, а разбить. Если три дня висит «параграфы 10–14», оставьте на завтра только параграф 10. Застревает обычно не человек, а слишком крупный пункт.

Нет. Начать можно бесплатно, рекламы нет, а Премиум — это разовая встроенная покупка, а не ежемесячное списание.

en.title: A cute study planner you will not abandon after a week
en.meta: Cute planners get dropped around day eight. Three rules keep one alive: plan once a week, three study items a day, a tick every evening. Mochi is free to start.
en.h1: How to keep a cute study planner going past the first week
en.lead: Planners are usually abandoned on day eight to ten. Not from laziness; by then the pretty page has turned into a record of everything not done.
en.answer: Plan once a week on Sunday evening, put no more than three study items a day with a concrete scope each, and tick what got done every evening. Move anything unfinished straight away instead of letting it pile up.
paras: The first week with a new planner is the pleasant one: themes, stickers, neat entries. Trouble starts when you write "prepare for the chemistry test" and "learn English", tasks with no end. They cannot be ticked, they hang there day after day, and a week later you do not want to open the page. Rule one: every item has a scope, such as "chemistry, section 12, problems 1–8" or "English, 20 words from unit 3".

Rule two: plan once a week, not every morning. On Sunday evening open the timetable, note what is due and when the tests are, and spread the preparation over Monday to Friday, three study items a day at most. If the week has a seminar and two tests, the rest honestly goes to a later list, not into Monday.

Rule three: the evening tick. Two minutes each night to tick what is done and move the rest to tomorrow's first slot or delete it. A planner with nothing to tick becomes a notebook. Mochi suits this format well: a separate study list, reminders, a little circle that is satisfying to tap after each item, a Home Screen widget that shows today without opening the app, and themes so the study list looks the way you like. Free to start, no ads.

loc.title: 10 coisas da casa que valem um registro de 'última vez'
loc.meta: Lençol, filtro, vermífugo, caixa d'água, óleo do carro: 10 coisas que valem anotar quando foi a última vez, e com que frequência. Mochi DoneStamp começa grátis.
loc.h1: As 10 coisas da casa que valem anotar quando foi a última vez (e de quanto em quanto tempo)
loc.lead: Quase ninguém esquece de lavar a louça. O que escapa é o que acontece a cada três ou seis meses: ninguém lembra se o refil do filtro foi trocado em março ou em agosto.
loc.answer: Vale anotar o que se repete em semanas ou meses e não deixa sinal visível: lençol, filtro do ar-condicionado, antipulgas, backup das fotos, refil do filtro de água, vermífugo, travesseiro, geladeira, caixa d'água e óleo do carro. A regra é contar o prazo a partir do dia em que você fez de verdade, não do dia marcado.
paras: Os quatro mais frequentes cabem num ciclo de semanas. Lençol a cada 1 a 2 semanas, puxando para 1 semana com pet na cama ou calor forte; filtro do ar-condicionado lavado a cada 2 a 4 semanas quando o aparelho roda todo dia. Antipulgas do pet todo mês, no dia que a embalagem indicar; backup das fotos do celular uma vez por mês e antes de qualquer viagem. Esses atrasam sem ninguém perceber, porque a casa não dá sinal de que passou do ponto.

Os outros seis demoram meses, e por isso somem da memória. Refil do filtro ou vela do purificador a cada 6 meses, ou antes se a vazão cair; vermífugo a cada 3 a 6 meses, no esquema que o veterinário passou; travesseiro lavado a cada 3 a 6 meses e trocado quando não volta ao formato. Geladeira com limpeza completa e checagem da borracha a cada 1 a 3 meses; caixa d'água limpa a cada 6 meses; óleo do carro no que vier primeiro, a quilometragem do manual ou 12 meses, porque óleo envelhece mesmo parado. Em todos eles o prazo conta a partir do dia em que foi feito, não do dia em que estava marcado.

O erro comum é marcar essas datas no calendário. O calendário avisa no dia 15 mesmo que você tenha trocado o filtro no dia 10, e o próximo aviso já nasce errado. O que funciona é registrar a conclusão e deixar o próximo prazo recomeçar dali: o Mochi DoneStamp faz exatamente isso, um toque guarda a hora exata, com ritmo aproximado ou exato de minutos a anos, lembrete local com Concluir e Adiar e widget na Tela de Início e de Bloqueio. Começa grátis, sem conta e sem anúncios.

en.title: 10 household things worth logging the last time you did them
en.meta: Sheets, filters, dewormer, water tank, the car's oil: ten household items worth a last-done log, and how often each recurs. Mochi DoneStamp is free to start.
en.h1: The 10 household things worth a last-time log, and how often each comes round
en.lead: Nobody forgets the dishes. What slips is anything on a three- or six-month cycle: nobody remembers whether the filter cartridge went in during March or August.
en.answer: Log whatever repeats in weeks or months and leaves no visible trace: sheets, the air-conditioner filter, flea treatment, photo backup, the water-filter cartridge, deworming, pillows, the fridge, the water tank and the car's oil. Count every interval from the day you actually did it, not the day it was scheduled.
paras: The four most frequent run on a cycle of weeks. Sheets every 1 to 2 weeks, closer to 1 with a pet on the bed or hot weather; the air-conditioner filter washed every 2 to 4 weeks when the unit runs daily. Flea treatment monthly, on the day the packet says; phone photo backup once a month and before any trip. These slip unnoticed because the house gives no sign that the interval has passed.

The other six take months, which is exactly why they vanish from memory. Water-filter cartridge or purifier candle every 6 months, sooner if the flow drops; deworming every 3 to 6 months on the vet's schedule; pillows washed every 3 to 6 months and replaced when they no longer spring back. Fridge fully cleaned with a seal check every 1 to 3 months; the rooftop water tank cleaned every 6 months; the car's oil at whichever comes first, the manual's mileage or 12 months, because oil ages even when the car sits. For all of them the clock starts on the day it was done, not the day it was due.

The usual mistake is putting these on the calendar. The calendar fires on the 15th even though you changed the filter on the 10th, so the next alert is already wrong. What works is logging the completion and letting the next due date restart from there: Mochi DoneStamp does exactly that, one tap stores the exact time, with an approximate or exact rhythm from minutes to years, local reminders with Done and Snooze, and Home and Lock Screen widgets. Free to start, no account, no ads.

When you do the task, log it on the spot, before the bucket or the packet goes away; that is where memory is lost.
Once a month, open the list and look only at what comes due in the next few weeks; the rest can stay quiet.

en.title: Logging when you last did it vs setting a reminder
en.meta: A reminder fires on the set date; a last-done log restarts from the day you really did it. Chores, car and health need the latter. Mochi DoneStamp is free.
en.h1: Why logging the last time beats a reminder: chores, car, health
en.lead: A reminder only knows the date arrived. It has no idea whether you did the thing. The real problem is rarely forgetting to do it; it is not knowing when you last did.
en.answer: Reminders suit things with a hard deadline, such as car tax or a doctor's appointment. For anything that can happen any day but needs to recur, such as changing sheets, cleaning the air conditioner or an oil change, log when you last did it and count the next interval from that real date.
paras: The difference is where the clock starts. A reminder counts from the date you set: clean the air conditioner a week early and next month's alert still fires on the old date, and after two or three snoozes nobody knows when it was really done. A last-done log shows the number you actually want, how many days it has been, and answers the question on the spot.

Split it into three groups. Home: sheets every 1 to 2 weeks, the air-conditioner filter washed every 2 to 4 weeks when it runs daily, a full air-conditioner service every 6 months, the water-filter cartridge every 6 months or per the manual. Car: an oil change at the manual's mileage or every 6 months, whichever comes first, and tyre pressure monthly. Health: a dental check every 6 months, a new toothbrush every 3 months, pet deworming every 3 to 6 months on the vet's advice. What they share is that two weeks late breaks nothing, while six months forgotten costs money.

The method is to log at the moment you finish, not when you happen to remember, because memory goes the moment the tools are put away. If you only remember days later, an approximate backdated entry beats a blank. Mochi DoneStamp works this way: one tap stores the exact time, approximate or exact rhythms run from minutes to years, the next due date restarts from the real finish, and there are Home and Lock Screen widgets. Free to start, no ads, no account.

Sort the rest into home, car and health and enter the last time you remember, roughly the month is enough.
Give each a rough interval from the numbers above, then adjust for your home: pets, dust, daily driving.
Log the moment you finish, before putting anything away; if a reminder also fired, tap Done, not Snooze.
Once a month, look only at what comes due in the next four weeks and ignore the rest.

With a calendar reminder, yes, by hand, and that is where most people give up. With a last-done log the next interval restarts from the real date on its own.
I forgot to log it when I finished. Now what?
Enter an approximate backdated entry as soon as you remember, such as early this month. It beats a blank, and you can correct it if a receipt or photo turns up.

loc.title: 接案怎麼分專案記帳，算出每個案子真的賺多少？
loc.meta: 接案賺多少，不是看入帳金額，是入帳扣掉材料、外包、交通之後剩下的數字。一案一本帳、三類成本各貼一個標籤，結案看淨額，下次報價就有依據。MoneyTag 免費開始，一次購買、不訂閱。
loc.h1: 分專案記帳：扣掉材料、外包、交通，才知道這個案子真的賺多少
loc.lead: 很多接案者把所有收入記在同一本帳，年底只知道總共收了多少，卻說不出哪一個案子其實是賠錢做的。
loc.answer: 每接一個案子就開一本獨立的帳，收入與支出只記在那一本；支出固定分成材料、外包、交通三類貼標籤，結案時「收入減支出」就是真實利潤，這個數字直接拿去修正下一次報價。
paras: 「這個案子入帳十萬」聽起來不錯，但扣掉找人分工的外包費、印刷與素材授權的材料費、來回客戶公司和場勘的交通費之後，剩下的可能只有一半多一點。生活帳和案子混在一起記，你看到的是「收到的錢」，不是「賺到的錢」，而報價是用賺到的錢去算的。

en.title: Split freelance books by project to see real profit
en.meta: A freelance job earns what is left after materials, subcontracting and travel. One ledger per job, three cost tags. MoneyTag is free to start, one-time unlock.
en.h1: Per-project bookkeeping: subtract materials, subcontractors and travel before you call it profit
en.lead: Most freelancers record every payment in one ledger, know the yearly total, and still cannot say which job they actually lost money on.
en.answer: Open a separate ledger the day you take a job and record only that job's income and expenses in it. Tag every expense as materials, subcontractor or travel. At the end, income minus expenses is the real profit, and that figure corrects your next quote.
paras: A six-figure invoice feels good until you subtract the person you paid to share the work, the printing and licensed assets, and the trips to the client's office and the site. What remains can be little more than half. When living expenses and client work sit in the same ledger, you are looking at money received, not money earned, and quotes have to be built on money earned.

The method is two moves: one ledger per job, and three fixed tags. Materials are costs that end with the job, such as printing, assets, licences and consumables. Subcontractor is anything you paid someone else to do. Travel is client visits, site checks and shipping. Keep the tag list at three, because a long list is the reason nobody tags consistently. When the job closes, read the net first, then check what share of income each tag took. On the next similar job, add those three shares back in before you add the margin you want.

MoneyTag is built for exactly this. Every project is its own ledger, and income minus expenses is that project's net. Any entry can carry a tag, and the Tags screen totals the same tag across all projects, so the cost type that keeps eating your margin is visible at once. Overseas clients paying in another currency are fine: each project keeps one base currency, and entries are converted with live or manual rates. Free to start; unlimited projects, tags and reports are a one-time purchase.

en.h1: Side-job income: a clean record that keeps private spending out
en.lead: Separating a side job from private money rarely fails for lack of discipline. It fails because both run through the same account. What needs separating is the record, not necessarily the account.
en.answer: Keep one ledger that holds only the side job: every payment with date, who paid and how, and every expense only if it would not exist without the job. Everything else stays out. What you eventually have to declare is set by your local rules; this page is about the recording method.
paras: The usual pattern: the client transfers to the personal account, materials go on the personal card, the trip there is paid in cash. Three months later nobody can tell which entries belonged to the side job. The shared account is not the problem. The problem is that there is no separate ledger where side-job entries land the same day.

What belongs in it: for each payment, the date, the amount, who paid and by what route (transfer, cash, payment service). For expenses, one question only: would this exist without the side job? If not, it goes in, with the receipt number in the note. Things that are both, like the phone or the internet, get a tag called Mixed and are not split on the spot. How much of them counts toward the job depends on the applicable rules and your situation; sort that out once a month against the official guidance or with an adviser, not entry by entry.

In MoneyTag each side job is its own project with its own ledger: income minus expenses is its net, and private spending never enters. Every entry has a note for client, payment route and receipt number, plus tags such as Materials, Travel or Mixed; the Tags screen totals the same tag across all projects. For handing over, export as CSV or PDF. Data stays in on-device storage. Free to start; unlimited projects, tags and reports are a one-time purchase.

Yes. One entry each, with dates, so midway through you know what has landed and what is still due, without confusing a quote with money earned.
Is MoneyTag a subscription?
No. Free to start; unlimited projects, tags and reports are a one-time purchase, no renewal. No subscription.

loc.title: Рукописные конспекты на iPad, которые потом находятся
loc.meta: Конспект от руки теряется без системы: тетрадь на курс, четыре цвета, PDF лекции рядом, печатный заголовок. 100 Notes Studio: бесплатный старт, разовая покупка.
loc.h1: Как вести рукописные конспекты на iPad, чтобы потом их находить
loc.lead: Сложность конспекта от руки не в том, чтобы его написать, а в том, что через месяц его невозможно найти. Решает это не приложение, а четыре договорённости с самим собой до начала семестра.
loc.answer: Одна тетрадь на курс, печатный заголовок с номером недели и темой на каждой странице, четыре постоянных цвета и PDF лекции, импортированный в ту же тетрадь, — при такой структуре любой рукописный конспект находится за десять секунд.
paras: Начните со структуры до первой лекции. На каждый курс — своя тетрадь или папка, внутри — страницы по неделям. Сверху каждой страницы печатными буквами пишите код курса, номер недели и тему: «Матан, нед. 3, пределы». Печатный заголовок распознаётся надёжнее беглого почерка, поэтому поиск по нему работает даже в самом неразборчивом конспекте.

Цвета нужны не для красоты, а как единая маркировка для всех предметов. Четырёх хватает: тёмно-синий — основной текст, красный — определения и то, что точно спросят, жёлтый — свои мысли и вопросы, оранжевый — связи с другими темами. Если в каждом предмете цвета значат разное, через месяц вы перестанете им доверять. Слайды лекций импортируйте как PDF в ту же тетрадь и пишите рядом с ними то, что преподаватель говорит вслух, а не то, что уже напечатано.

Все эти привычки держатся на приложении, где поиск видит ваш почерк. В 100 Notes Studio распознавание рукописного текста выполняется прямо на устройстве: ищите по заголовкам, тексту, рукописным записям и вложениям без подключения к сети. PDF лекции импортируется в тетрадь и размечается выделением, подчёркиванием и рукописными пометками, а аудиозапись лекции прикрепляется к той странице, на которой вы её начали. Вложенные папки, теги и автоматически нумеруемое оглавление собирают семестр в одну структуру.

steps: До первой лекции создайте тетрадь на каждый курс и договоритесь с собой о четырёх цветах — запишите их значение на первой странице.

Бесплатный режим включает редактор и одну активную тетрадь с неограниченным числом страниц, разблокировка — разовая.

Четыре, и одни и те же во всех предметах: основной текст, определения, свои мысли, связи с другими темами. Больше четырёх — и значение цветов перестаёт помниться.

en.title: Handwritten iPad lecture notes you can actually find later
en.meta: Handwritten notes get lost without a system: a notebook per course, four fixed colours, lecture PDF alongside. 100 Notes Studio: free to start, one-time unlock.
en.h1: How to structure handwritten lecture notes on iPad so you find them again
en.lead: Writing the notes is the easy part. The hard part is finding one page of them a month later. That is fixed by four rules you set before term starts, not by the app.
en.answer: One notebook per course, a printed heading with week number and topic on every page, four colours that always mean the same thing, and the lecture PDF imported into the same notebook — with that structure any handwritten page turns up in ten seconds.
paras: Set the structure before the first lecture. Each course gets its own notebook or folder, with pages grouped by week. At the top of every page, print the course code, week number and topic in block capitals: "Calc, wk 3, limits". Block capitals are recognised far more reliably than cursive, so search on the heading works even when the body of the page is a scrawl.

Colours are a filing code, not decoration, and the code has to be identical across every subject. Four is enough: dark blue for the main notes, red for definitions and anything likely to be examined, yellow for your own thoughts and questions, orange for links to other topics. If colours mean different things in different courses you will stop trusting them within a month. Import the lecture slides as a PDF into the same notebook and write beside them only what the lecturer says out loud, never what is already printed.

All of this depends on an app whose search can read your handwriting. In 100 Notes Studio, handwriting recognition runs on the device, and search covers titles, body text, handwriting and attachments without a network connection. Lecture PDFs import into the notebook and take highlights, underlines and handwritten notes, and an audio recording stays attached to the page where you started it. Nested folders, tags and an auto-numbered table of contents hold a whole semester in one structure.

At the top of every new page, print the course code, week number and topic in block capitals.
Import the slide PDF before the lecture; during it, write only what is not already on the slides.
At the end of each week, go back through the pages and mark in red the three things most likely to be examined.
Once a week, test the system with search: type a term you only ever wrote by hand. If it does not come up, fix the heading or rewrite that spot legibly.

It does not suit anyone who needs shared editing with classmates or cloud sync across platforms. The free version includes the editor and one active notebook with unlimited pages; the unlock is a one-time purchase.
faq: How many colours should I use?
Four, and the same four in every subject: main notes, definitions, your own thoughts, links to other topics. Past four, you stop remembering what each one means.
How do I search handwritten notes if my handwriting is messy?
Print the headings in block capitals; search on those is reliable. In 100 Notes Studio recognition runs on the device and covers titles, body text, handwriting and attachments.

No. The free version includes the editor, one active notebook with unlimited pages and 2 of the 100 styles. More notebooks, the remaining styles, vector PDF export, page history and encrypted backup come with a single one-time purchase. No ads, no account.

loc.title: Notas a mano en iPad con el método Cornell
loc.meta: Los apuntes a mano se repasan si la página está pensada para ello: preguntas, notas, resumen y PDF juntos. 100 Notes Studio: gratis para empezar, un solo pago.
loc.h1: Tomar notas a mano en iPad: un método de apuntes que luego sí se repasan
loc.lead: Casi nadie vuelve a leer sus apuntes porque la página se escribió para copiar, no para repasar. El método Cornell arregla eso antes de escribir la primera línea.
loc.answer: Divide cada página en tres zonas antes de la clase: una columna izquierda estrecha para preguntas, el bloque principal para notas y cinco líneas abajo para el resumen. Repasar consiste en tapar la derecha y responder a la izquierda; con el PDF de la clase en el mismo cuaderno no hace falta cambiar de app.
paras: El método Cornell no es una plantilla, es un reparto de la página: la columna izquierda ocupa más o menos un tercio del ancho y se deja vacía durante la clase; el bloque derecho recoge lo que explica el profesor; las cinco líneas finales se rellenan ese mismo día con un resumen de dos frases. En un cuaderno digital puedes trazar esas líneas con la regla una vez y duplicar la página, o simplemente marcar la columna con una línea vertical al empezar cada hoja.

Lo que de verdad hace que se repase viene después de clase: antes de 24 horas vuelves a la página, escribes en la columna izquierda la pregunta que responde cada bloque de notas y resumes abajo. Al repasar, tapas la derecha y contestas en voz alta. Si el profesor cuelga el PDF de los apuntes, impórtalo en el mismo cuaderno y escribe al lado sólo lo que dice y no está en las diapositivas; subrayar lo que ya está impreso no es tomar notas.

Para que el método funcione en el iPad, la app tiene que dejar escribir sobre el PDF y buscar luego en tu propia letra. 100 Notes Studio importa documentos PDF y permite resaltar, subrayar y añadir escritura a mano en la misma página; el reconocimiento de escritura funciona en el dispositivo y la búsqueda cubre títulos, contenido, trazos y adjuntos. Las preguntas de la columna izquierda pueden pasar a fichas enlazadas y repetirse con repetición espaciada FSRS, y el audio de la clase queda unido a la página donde empezaste a grabar.

Durante la clase escribe sólo en el bloque derecho; si hay PDF de apuntes, impórtalo y anota al lado lo que se dice y no está impreso.
Esa misma tarde escribe en la columna izquierda una pregunta por cada bloque de notas.
Rellena el resumen de abajo en dos frases, sin mirar las notas.

loc.fits: 100 Notes Studio encaja con estudiantes que escriben a mano en iPad y quieren apuntes, PDF de clase, audio y fichas de repaso en un cuaderno privado que funciona sin conexión. No encaja si necesitas editar apuntes en equipo o sincronizarlos en la nube entre plataformas. La versión gratuita incluye el editor completo y un cuaderno con páginas ilimitadas; la compra es única.
faq: ¿Cuánto debe ocupar la columna de preguntas?
Más o menos un tercio del ancho. Si es más estrecha no caben preguntas completas y acabas escribiendo palabras sueltas que luego no entiendes.
Si el profesor da los apuntes en PDF, ¿para qué escribir a mano?
El PDF es la parte impresa; a mano va lo que se dice en clase, las preguntas de la izquierda y el resumen. Importa el PDF al cuaderno y usa el margen o la página contigua para eso.
¿100 Notes Studio es de suscripción?

No. La versión gratuita incluye las 29 herramientas de escritura, anotación de PDF, audio, búsqueda de escritura y modo de estudio, con 1 cuaderno de páginas ilimitadas y 2 de los 100 estilos. Una compra única opcional añade más cuadernos, los 100 estilos, exportación vectorial a PDF, historial de versiones y copia cifrada. Sin cuenta ni publicidad.

en.title: Cornell notes by hand on iPad: a method you will revise from
en.meta: Handwritten class notes get revised when the page is built for it: question column, notes, summary, PDF together. 100 Notes Studio: free to start, one-time buy.
en.h1: Taking notes by hand on iPad: a class-notes method that gets revised
en.lead: Most notes are never read again because the page was written for copying, not for revising. The Cornell method fixes that before the first line goes down.
en.answer: Split every page into three zones before class: a narrow left column for questions, the main block for notes and five lines at the bottom for a summary. Revising means covering the right side and answering the left; with the class PDF in the same notebook there is no app to switch to.
paras: Cornell is not a template, it is a division of the page: the left column takes roughly a third of the width and stays empty during class; the right block holds what the lecturer explains; the last five lines are filled the same day with a two-sentence summary. In a digital notebook you draw those lines once with the ruler and reuse the page, or just mark the column with one vertical line as you start each sheet.

What actually makes revision happen comes after class: within 24 hours you return to the page, write in the left column the question each block of notes answers, and summarise at the bottom. To revise, cover the right side and answer out loud. If the lecturer posts the notes as a PDF, import it into the same notebook and write beside it only what was said and is not on the slides; underlining what is already printed is not note-taking.

For the method to work on iPad, the app has to let you write over the PDF and later search your own handwriting. 100 Notes Studio imports PDFs and lets you highlight, underline and add handwriting on the same page; handwriting recognition runs on the device and search covers titles, body text, strokes and attachments. The questions from the left column can become linked flashcards reviewed with FSRS spaced repetition, and class audio stays attached to the page where you started recording.

Whether the class PDF imports into the same notebook and takes handwriting on top

steps: Before class, open a portrait A4 page and use the ruler to draw a vertical line a third of the way across and a horizontal line five lines from the bottom.
During class write only in the right block; if there is a PDF of the notes, import it and write beside it what is said but not printed.
That same afternoon, write one question in the left column for each block of notes.
Fill in the bottom summary in two sentences without looking at the notes.
Two days later, cover the right side, answer the left-column questions and mark in red the ones you missed: those become flashcards.

en.fits: 100 Notes Studio fits students who write by hand on iPad and want notes, class PDFs, audio and revision cards in one private notebook that works offline. It does not fit anyone who needs to edit notes as a team or sync them in the cloud across platforms. The free version includes the full editor and one notebook with unlimited pages; the purchase is one-time.
faq: How wide should the question column be?
About a third of the width. Any narrower and full questions do not fit, so you end up with single words you cannot interpret later.
If the lecturer hands out the notes as a PDF, why write by hand?
The PDF is the printed part; by hand goes what is said in class, the left-column questions and the summary. Import the PDF into the notebook and use the margin or the facing page for that.

No. The free version includes the 29 writing tools, PDF annotation, audio, handwriting search and study mode, with 1 notebook of unlimited pages and 2 of the 100 styles. en.title: Handwritten iPad notes that are easy to reread before exams
en.meta: Handwritten notes fail at revision when the page was never divided: heading, question column, 3 colours, slides alongside. 100 Notes Studio: free, one-time buy.
en.h1: Handwritten notes on iPad that are easy to reread: page layout, colours and slide PDFs
en.lead: The problem with handwritten notes is not ugly handwriting. It is opening them the week before an exam and not knowing where to start. Dividing the page before you write fixes that more than any pen does.
en.answer: Divide the page into three zones before writing: heading and date at the top, a narrow left column for questions, the right side for content. Use only three colours, each meaning one thing in every subject, and import the slide PDF into the same notebook as the notes. Revision then becomes a page-by-page pass that takes ten minutes.
paras: Start with the page layout. Every page gets a heading printed in block capitals at the top, such as subject, week and topic, because block capitals are found by search far more reliably than cursive. Then draw a vertical line so the left column is about a third of the page; leave it empty during class, write content only on the right, and keep four or five lines at the bottom for a summary. When every page shares one layout, your eyes know where to look the moment you open it to revise.

Colours signal the type of information, not decoration. Three are enough: a main colour for content, red for definitions and likely exam material, a third for your own questions and thoughts. The meanings must stay the same in every subject; change them around and you stop trusting the colours within a month. Import the lecturer's slides as a PDF into the same notebook as your notes, then write beside them only what was said and is not on the slide. Highlighting what is already printed is not note-taking.

This only works when the app can find your handwriting. 100 Notes Studio recognises handwriting and searches on the device without a connection, across titles, text, handwriting and attachments. Slide PDFs import for highlights, underlines and handwriting on the same page. Questions from the left column can become flashcards and cloze cards reviewed on an FSRS spaced-repetition schedule, and audio recorded in class stays attached to the page where it started, so it plays back with that page's notes.

steps: Create one notebook or folder per subject and write the meaning of your three colours on its first page.
On every new page, print the heading in block capitals at the top and draw the one-third left column with the ruler.
Import the slide PDF before class; during class write only what the lecturer adds, beside the slide or on the right side of the page.
The same day after class, write a question in the left column for each section of content and a two-sentence summary at the bottom.
Every weekend, cover the right side and answer the left column; turn anything you cannot answer into a review card, then search a handwritten word to confirm the app finds it.

en.fits: 100 Notes Studio fits students who write by hand on iPad and want notes, slide PDFs, class audio and flashcards in one notebook with no account and no monthly fee. It does not fit anyone who needs to edit notes with classmates in real time or sync through the cloud across platforms. The free version has the full set of writing tools and one notebook with unlimited pages; a one-time purchase unlocks the rest.
faq: How many colours should I use in my notes?
Three: a main colour, one for definitions and likely exam material, one for your own questions. Keep the meanings the same in every subject; more than that and you forget which colour means what.
If the lecturer already gives slides as a PDF, do I still need to write by hand?
Yes, but only what the lecturer adds and your own questions. Import the slides into the notebook and write beside them or on the next page; what is already printed does not need copying.
Is 100 Notes Studio a monthly subscription?

No. The free version includes 29 writing tools, PDF markup, page audio, handwriting search and study mode, with 1 notebook of unlimited pages and 2 of the 100 styles. A one-time purchase adds more notebooks, all 100 styles, vector PDF export, version history and encrypted backup. No account, no ads.

en.title: Claude usage across several accounts: which one to continue on
en.meta: With several Claude accounts, the one with more left is not always the one that lasts. Line up each account's 5-hour and weekly limits and exact reset times on one widget, and switching stops being guesswork.
en.h1: Claude usage with several accounts: look at which one resets first
en.lead: One account is out, another still has room, and you cannot tell which will last longer. That is where people with several accounts get stuck.
en.answer: With several Claude accounts, put each account's 5-hour limit, weekly limit and exact reset time side by side and sort by 5-hour reset; the account to continue on comes up first, without signing in to each one.
paras: Many people searching for Claude usage run more than one account: a work account from the company, a personal one they pay for, or a Pro and a Max side by side. Each account counts down its 5-hour session limit and weekly limit separately, so the account with more left is not always the one that lasts. An account near its weekly cap can stop you halfway even with a full 5-hour window, which is why comparing accounts means reading both limits and both reset times.

UsageNow puts every account on one screen: work and personal, Pro and Max, side by side, sorted by 5-hour reset, weekly reset, highest or lowest usage, name or service, or dragged into your own order. On Home Screen and Lock Screen widgets you can flip through each account directly, and a tap on the widget refreshes it when you want the latest numbers.

The moment to switch can come from an alert instead of memory. Set the percentage you care about, like 90 or 98, for the 5-hour limit, the weekly limit or all limits; each alert fires once per limit and cycle. Turn on the reset alert and you know when the account that ran out is back. Sign-in happens on each service's own login page and stays in the device's Keychain; there is no UsageNow server and no account to create.

그래서 확인하는 대신 알림을 받는 쪽이 낫습니다. UsageNow에서는 5시간 한도, 주간 한도 또는 모든 한도를 고른 뒤 신경 쓰이는 퍼센트를 직접 입력해 알림을 만들 수 있고, 원하는 만큼 추가할 수 있습니다. 알림은 한도별로 주기마다 한 번만 울리므로 잠금 화면이 알림으로 가득 차지 않습니다. 예를 들어 90에서는 지금 단계를 정리할 시점을, 98에서는 지금까지의 작업을 커밋할 시점을 알리게 둘 수 있습니다.

The time until each reset counts down live on Home Screen and Lock Screen widgets and Apple Watch complications, with the exact reset time in your local format. Sign-in happens on each service's official login page and stays only in the device's Keychain.

loc.h1: 待辦事項 App 總是用不久？挑一個你每天會打開的
loc.lead: 下載了好幾個待辦事項 App 卻都沒在用，通常不是你不夠自律，而是那個 App 沒有讓你想打開它。
loc.answer: 看得到、打勾有感覺、每天只放幾件事——同時做到這三件事的待辦清單，才會被每天打開；功能多寡反而是次要的。
paras: 第一個條件是看得到。藏在第三頁資料夾裡的 App，再好用也會被忘記。把今天的清單放到主畫面小工具，每次解鎖手機就會看到，等於每天自動提醒自己好幾次，不必再靠記性去打開它。
第二個條件是完成有感覺。劃掉一行、點一下圓圈、進度往前走，這些小回饋是每天願意回來的理由。外觀也算在內：主畫面是粉嫩色系，放一個灰色表格風的 App 會很突兀，有喜歡的主題，才會願意讓小工具一直留在那裡。
第三個條件是每天的量要小。清單越寫越長，就會從工具變成罪惡感來源。每天只放四、五件真的要做的事，其他的另外放一份清單，週末再看。Mochi 就是照這個想法做的：輕點小圓圈完成打勾，有 101 款主題、桌面小工具和 Apple Watch App；免費版可以有 2 個清單、每個最多 4 個項目。

en.title: To-do list app you stop using? Pick one you keep opening
en.meta: A to-do list app gets abandoned when it is out of sight, finishing feels like nothing and the list keeps growing. Check the widget, the tick and a daily cap. Mochi is free to start.
en.h1: Stopped using every to-do list app? Pick one you keep opening
en.lead: If you have installed several to-do list apps and use none of them, the issue is usually not discipline. The app simply never made you want to open it.
en.answer: Visible, satisfying to tick, and small enough to finish each day: a to-do list that does all three gets opened daily. The number of features matters far less.
paras: The first condition is visibility. An app buried in a folder on page three gets forgotten, however good it is. Put today's list in a Home Screen widget and you see it every time you unlock your phone, which is several reminders a day without relying on memory.

The second is a finish that feels like something. Crossing out a line, tapping a circle, watching progress move: these small returns are why people come back. Looks count too. On a pastel Home Screen, a grey spreadsheet-style app sticks out, and a theme you like is a reason to keep the widget there.

The third is a small daily list. A list that only grows turns from a tool into a source of guilt. Keep four or five things you will really do today and park the rest on a second list for the weekend. Mochi is built around that idea: tap the little circle to check off, 101 themes, Home Screen widgets and Apple Watch; the free version has 2 lists of up to 4 tasks each.

en.answer: Choose a planner to keep plans and records, a to-do list to get today done. The part you open every day is today's tasks, so that is the part worth making cute.

What you check every single day is today's tasks. If that list is pretty, always visible on the Home Screen and cleared with a tap, it changes how the day feels. Many people keep the month on paper or in a calendar and only today's four tasks in a to-do app.

Mochi is a to-do list built for exactly that daily part. Add tasks and tap the little circle when you finish. It has 101 themes, Home Screen widgets and Apple Watch support, and the free version gives you 2 lists of up to 4 tasks each.

en.title: A cute to-do list you keep using in exam season
en.meta: Cute to-do lists are the first thing dropped in exam season. Split by week, cap the day at four and keep it in a widget, and it survives. Mochi is free to start.
en.h1: How to make a cute to-do list you keep using in exam season
en.lead: A pretty to-do list is fun on a normal week, and it is usually the first thing abandoned when exams pile up.
en.answer: Four tasks a day at most, two lists (today and this week), and a Home Screen widget so it is always in view. Keep those three and the list survives a busy week.
paras: A common reason to-do lists die in exam season is that they get too long. Write every chapter of every subject into one list and it overwhelms you the moment you open it, so you stop opening it. Keep only the four things you can finish today on Today, and the rest on a This week list.

The second factor is where the list sits. A list you can only see inside the app gets forgotten on busy days. A Home Screen widget shows the next task every time you look at your phone, and the small finish of tapping a circle and seeing the line crossed out carries you to the next one.

The third is when you decorate. Choose themes and emoji on the weekend; on weekdays, only add and tick. Mochi is a cute checklist where you add tasks and tap the little circle, with 101 themes, Home Screen widgets and Apple Watch support; the free version gives 2 lists of up to 4 tasks each.

loc.title: 小一注音闖關前在家怎麼複習？認讀、拼讀、聲調三件事的練法
loc.meta: 小一注音教學期快結束時，不少學校會用闖關或小考確認孩子學會了沒。在家不用出考卷：把認讀、拼讀、聲調拆開，每天各練幾分鐘就夠。文末說明 Lumi注音星球 可以接在哪一步。
loc.h1: 小一注音闖關前，在家怎麼複習認讀、拼讀與聲調
loc.lead: 注音教學期的尾聲，不少學校會用闖關、小考或朗讀確認孩子的程度。在家複習不必模擬考試，把要確認的三件事拆開，每天各練一小段，孩子比較不會緊張。
loc.answer: 把複習拆成認讀、拼讀、聲調三件事，每天各練三到四分鐘：先聽音找符號，再拼兩三個音，最後同一個音連唸四聲。
paras: 認讀是看到符號唸得出來、聽到聲音找得到符號。容易混的通常是長得像或聲音接近的組合，例如ㄅ和ㄆ、ㄓ和ㄗ、ㄣ和ㄥ。複習時不用把 37 個從頭唸到尾，挑孩子這週最常錯的三到五個就好。
拼讀是把聲母、介音、韻母接成一個音，例如ㄒ、ㄧ、ㄠ接起來是ㄒㄧㄠ。孩子如果每個符號都認得卻拼不出來，先放慢：大人唸一個音，孩子指出它由哪幾個符號組成，再反過來讓孩子自己拼。
聲調最容易在闖關時被抓出來，尤其是二聲和三聲。同一個音連唸四聲（ㄇㄚ：媽、麻、馬、罵）再配手勢比高低，比單獨背調號有用。Lumi注音星球 的四種玩法剛好對應這幾步，可以免費開始使用。

en.title: Learn Zhuyin for kids: a 10-minute home review of symbols, blending and tones
en.meta: Near the end of the first-grade Zhuyin unit in Taiwan, many schools check reading, blending and tones. At home you don't need a mock test: practise each skill for a few minutes a day. A routine, and where Lumi Bopomofo fits.
en.h1: Learn Zhuyin for kids: reviewing symbols, blending and tones at home
en.lead: Toward the end of the Zhuyin unit, many Taiwanese schools check progress with a short quiz, a reading or a game-style challenge. Families anywhere can use the same three checks at home without turning practice into a test.
en.answer: Split review into three skills (reading symbols, blending and tones) and spend three or four minutes on each: find the symbol for a sound, blend two or three syllables, then say one syllable in all four tones.
paras: Reading means saying a symbol when you see it and finding it when you hear it. Mix-ups usually come in look-alike or sound-alike pairs such as ㄅ and ㄆ, ㄓ and ㄗ, or ㄣ and ㄥ. You don't need to run through all 37 symbols; pick the three to five your child missed most this week.

Blending joins an initial, a medial and a final into one syllable: ㄒ, ㄧ and ㄠ become ㄒㄧㄠ. If a child knows every symbol but can't blend, slow down: you say a syllable, they point to the symbols inside it, then swap roles and let them build it.

Tones are where most mistakes show up, especially the second and third tones. Saying one syllable in all four tones (ㄇㄚ: mā, má, mǎ, mà) with a hand gesture for the pitch works better than memorising tone marks. Lumi Bopomofo's four games map onto these steps, and it is free to start.

steps: Write the three to five symbols your child missed most this week on sticky notes.
Reading, 3 minutes: you say a sound and your child finds the note; then swap roles.
Blending, 3 minutes: take two or three syllables from their reader, split them apart, then put them back together.
Tones, 3 minutes: say one syllable in all four tones and repeat the one they missed with a hand gesture.
Finish with a minute of whatever practice your child picks, and start tomorrow with today's misses.

en.fits: Lumi Bopomofo covers these steps for young children: Feed the Friends (listen and pick the right symbol), Sound Train (blend initial + medial + final into a syllable), Tone Coaster (the four tones) and Magic Tracing (trace each stroke). Completely ad-free, no sign-up, English and Chinese interface.
faq: What if my child didn't pass the school's Zhuyin check?

Work out which kind of mistake it was: not recognising symbols, not blending, or wrong tones. Each needs different practice, and a few minutes a day on the weakest one usually helps more than redoing everything.
How long should we practise each day?
For a first grader, about ten minutes at a regular time is plenty. Short and daily beats long and occasional.

loc.title: 爸媽自己注音不熟，怎麼陪孩子練？不用當發音示範的做法
loc.meta: 陪小一孩子寫注音作業，才發現自己ㄓㄗ、ㄣㄥ也唸不準？大人不必當發音老師：發音示範交給音檔或有語音的練習工具，大人負責陪孩子聽、找、拼，記下常錯的音。
loc.h1: 爸媽自己注音不熟，怎麼陪孩子練注音？
loc.lead: 很多大人的注音是小時候學的，多年沒用，聲調和相近的音難免不確定。陪練的重點不是大人發音標準，而是每天陪孩子聽、找、拼一小段。
loc.answer: 大人不用當發音示範：讓孩子聽標準的音、自己找出符號再拼起來，大人負責陪伴、計時，記下孩子常錯的音就好。
paras: 大人最常不確定的，多半是相近的音：ㄓㄔㄕ和ㄗㄘㄙ、ㄣ和ㄥ，還有二聲和三聲。這很正常，日常說話本來就常混著唸。與其擔心自己唸錯、教錯，不如把示範發音交給老師、課本附的音檔或有語音的練習工具。
大人可以做的事反而更重要：固定每天的時段、一次只練幾分鐘、把孩子常錯的音記下來，隔天先複習。孩子唸錯時先別急著糾正，讓他再聽一次正確的音、自己比比看，比較不會讓練習變成壓力。
如果學校或安親班有注音練習本，可以照它的順序走，在家只要補上「聽」和「拼」的次數。Lumi注音星球 會播放聲音讓孩子選出正確的注音，也有拼音、聲調和筆順的練習，可以免費開始使用。

en.title: How to teach my child Zhuyin when I can't read it myself
en.meta: Many parents abroad want their child to read Zhuyin (Bopomofo) but never learned it, or forgot it. You don't need to model the sounds yourself: how to practise together, and where Lumi Bopomofo fits.
en.h1: How to teach your child Zhuyin when you can't read it yourself
en.lead: Plenty of parents, especially outside Taiwan, never learned Zhuyin or learned it decades ago. Your job isn't to pronounce every sound perfectly; it's to build a short daily habit of listening, finding and blending.
en.answer: You don't need to be the pronunciation model: let your child hear correct audio, find the symbols and blend them, while you keep time, keep it light and note the sounds they miss.
paras: The sounds adults are least sure about are usually the close pairs (ㄓㄔㄕ versus ㄗㄘㄙ, ㄣ versus ㄥ) and the second versus the third tone. Instead of worrying about teaching them wrong, hand the modelling to recordings: a teacher, a textbook's audio or a practice app with sound.

What you add matters more: a fixed time each day, a few minutes per session, and a list of the sounds your child missed so tomorrow starts with them. When your child gets one wrong, play the correct sound again and let them compare before you correct.

If your child attends a weekend Chinese school, follow its order and add more listening and blending at home. Lumi Bopomofo plays a sound and lets your child pick the right symbol, and has games for blending, tones and stroke order. It is free to start, and the interface is in English and Chinese.

en.fits: Lumi Bopomofo suits parents who want to help but aren't sure of the sounds: Feed the Friends lets your child listen and pick the right symbol, while Sound Train, Tone Coaster and Magic Tracing cover blending, the four tones and strokes. Completely ad-free, collects no personal data, no sign-up, progress stays on the device.
faq: Can I teach Zhuyin if I can't read it?
Yes. Your role is to organise the practice and keep it going, not to be the most accurate speaker. Let recordings model the sounds and check anything unclear in the Ministry of Education handbook.
Should I correct every mistake straight away?
Not always. Playing the correct sound again and letting your child compare often works better than direct correction, and keeps practice from feeling like pressure.
Does Lumi Bopomofo have an English interface?
Yes. The interface is in English and Chinese, so parents who don't read Chinese can follow along.
